userStories.summary: Display Leave Balance in a Consistent Decimal Format
userStories.description: As an employee, I want my leave balance to be displayed in the same decimal format across all pages so that I can easily understand my available leave without seeing different representations of the same value.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: A single decimal format is used across all pages. The same value is displayed consistently (e.g., 4.5 d everywhere or 4.50 d everywhere). Formatting follows approved UI/UX guidelines. Updates and refreshes retain the same format. Only display formatting changes; calculations remain unchanged.

testCases.expectedResult: The quantity of the item should update successfully in the cart. The subtotal and total price in the cart should accurately reflect the new quantity. No error messages or warnings should be displayed.
steps: 1. Launch the Flipkart application by navigating to "https://www.flipkart.com/".
2. Log in using the provided credentials: username 'pratheepa@qaoncloud.com' and password '••••••••'. (Note: Global Login is used to bypass OTP limitations for this test).
3. In the search bar, search for a readily available product (e.g., "smartphone").
4. Select a product from the search results and add it to the cart. If the cart already contains items, proceed to the next step.
5. Navigate to the 'Cart' page by clicking on the cart icon, typically located in the top right corner of the page.
6. On the Cart page, locate the product for which you intend to update the quantity.
7. Identify the quantity selector (usually a dropdown or +/- buttons) next to the product name/details.
8. Click on the quantity selector and choose a new quantity that is higher than the current quantity but still within the available stock (e.g., if current is 1, select 2 or 3).
9. Observe the page for automatic update or click an 'Update' button if one is present.
10. Verify that the quantity displayed for the item has been successfully updated to the newly selected value.

uiTestingReports.correctedReport:
## Corrected UI Report

**Application Module:** Online Shop Instructions Modal

This report outlines the corrected UI specification for the "How to Use the Online Shop" modal, addressing all previously identified issues to ensure a clean, professional, and accurate user experience.

---

### Spelling and Grammar Issues Corrected

The following text elements have been updated to reflect correct spelling, grammar, and word usage:

*   **Modal Title:**
    *   **Text:** "How to Use the Online Shop" (No change required, already correct).
*   **Instructional Text (Bullet Points):**
    *   **1. Browse our products and select the items you want to buy.**
        *   **Correction 1:** Changed `product's` to **`products`** (plural).
        *   **Correction 2:** Changed `by` to **`buy`**.
    *   **2. Add your chosen items to the cart and proceed to checkout.**
        *   **Correction 1:** Changed `chossen` to **`chosen`**.
        *   **Correction 2:** Changed `ceckout` to **`checkout`**.
    *   **3. Complete the payment and receive your order confirmation email.**
        *   **Correction 1:** Changed `Compleat` to **`Complete`**.
        *   **Correction 2:** Changed `recive` to **`receive`**.
        *   **Correction 3:** Changed `cofirmation` to **`confirmation`**.
*   **Thank You Message:**
    *   **Text:** "Thank you for shopping with us!" (No change required, already correct).
*   **"OK" Button:**
    *   **Text:** "OK" (No change required, already correct).

### Layout Issues Corrected

*   No UI layout issues were detected in the original analysis. The current layout, including element positioning, spacing, and sizing within the modal, is considered appropriate and aligned with design best practices. All elements remain clearly visible, well-aligned, and provide a balanced visual hierarchy.

### Visual Consistency Summary

The corrected UI maintains strong visual consistency across all elements within the modal and with the broader application design.

*   **Modal Structure:** The modal retains its distinct white background, subtle drop shadow, and a semi-transparent overlay to ensure focus on the instructional content. The header bar with a prominent title and close button remains visually consistent.
*   **Typography:** All text elements (title, bullet points, thank you message, button text) adhere to the application's established font families, sizes, and weights, ensuring readability and a consistent brand appearance.
*   **Interactive Elements:** The "OK" button maintains its grey background, white text, and rounded corners, consistent with other interactive elements within the application. The close "X" icon also maintains its expected appearance and functionality.
*   **Spacing and Alignment:** Consistent internal padding, line spacing, and horizontal alignment of text and button elements contribute to a clean, uncluttered presentation.

This corrected UI specification ensures that the "How to Use the Online Shop" modal provides clear, accurate, and professional guidance to users, enhancing the overall user experience.

As a registered user, I want to securely log in to the AutomatiQA platform so that I can access its features and manage my testing assets.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am on the login page, When I enter valid credentials and click 'Login', Then I should be authenticated and redirected to the project dashboard.
• Given I am on the login page, When I enter invalid credentials and click 'Login', Then I should see an error message indicating invalid credentials.
• Given I am on the login page, When I leave required fields (e.g., username, password) empty and click 'Login', Then I should see validation errors for the empty fields.
• Given I am logged in, When my session expires or I log out, Then I should be prompted to log in again to access the system.
• The login process must use secure protocols (e.g., HTTPS) and protect user credentials.

userStories.description: As a user with appropriate permissions, I want to create a new project within AutomatiQA so that I can organize my test automation efforts for a specific application or product.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am on the project management page and have 'Create Project' permissions, When I click 'Create New Project', enter a unique project name and description, and click 'Save', Then the new project should be created successfully and appear in my project list.
• Given I am on the project management page, When I attempt to create a project with a name that already exists, Then I should receive an error message indicating that project names must be unique.
• Given I am on the project management page, When I attempt to create a project with an empty project name, Then I should receive a validation error.
• Only users with the 'Project Creator' role (or similar) should be able to create new projects.

• Given I am logged in and navigate to the project selection screen, Then I should see a list of all projects that have been assigned to me.
• Each project in the list should display its name and a brief description.
• I should not be able to see or access projects to which I have not been explicitly assigned.
• Clicking on a project in the list should navigate me to that project's dashboard or overview.

userStories.summary: Configure Jira Integration for a Project
userStories.description: As a project administrator, I want to configure the integration with Jira for a specific project so that AutomatiQA can access and import user stories from Jira.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am in a specific project's settings and have 'Admin' permissions, When I provide valid Jira URL, API token/credentials, and the Jira Project Key, Then the integration should be successfully established and verified.
• Given the integration is configured, When I attempt to import Jira stories, Then the system should use the stored configuration and credentials to connect to Jira.
• If invalid Jira credentials or an inaccessible Jira instance is provided, Then an appropriate error message should be displayed, and the integration should not be saved.

userStories.description: As a user, I want to import user stories from a connected Jira project so that I can use them as a basis for generating acceptance criteria and test scenarios.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given Jira integration is successfully configured for my current project, When I initiate the 'Import Jira Stories' action, Then a list of available user stories from the connected Jira project should be displayed.
• Given I have selected specific Jira user stories from the displayed list, When I confirm the import, Then these stories should be imported into AutomatiQA, retaining their original Jira IDs and key details (e.g., summary, description).
• Each imported story in AutomatiQA should have a clear link or reference back to its corresponding Jira issue.
• The system should handle cases where a Jira story has already been imported, preventing duplicates or offering update options.

userStories.description: As a QA Lead or Business Analyst, I want to use AI to generate comprehensive acceptance criteria for an imported Jira user story so that I can quickly define clear expectations for testing.
userStories.summary: Generate AI-Powered Acceptance Criteria for a User Story
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I have selected an imported Jira user story, When I trigger the 'Generate Acceptance Criteria' action, Then the AI model should process the story's description and propose a set of acceptance criteria.
• The generated acceptance criteria should be displayed in a review interface, allowing me to accept, modify, or reject individual criteria.
• I should be able to manually add, edit, or delete acceptance criteria even after AI generation.
• When I finalize the criteria, Then they should be saved and permanently associated with the selected user story.
• The AI generation process should complete within an acceptable time frame (e.g., less than 3 seconds).

• Given I have a user story with finalized acceptance criteria, When I trigger the 'Generate AI Scenarios' action, Then the AI model should propose multiple, distinct test scenarios that cover all associated acceptance criteria.
• The generated scenarios should be displayed for review, allowing me to select, modify, or deselect them.
• I should be able to save the selected AI-generated scenarios, ensuring they are associated with the originating user story and its acceptance criteria.
• Each generated scenario should clearly outline a sequence of steps and an expected outcome.
• The system should ensure that AI-generated scenarios are saved in association with their respective user stories as per business rules.
userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to use AI to generate detailed test scenarios based on a user story and its acceptance criteria so that I can efficiently plan my testing efforts.
userStories.summary: Generate AI-Powered Test Scenarios from User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to generate concrete test cases from the approved test scenarios so that I can create executable tests for automation or manual execution.
userStories.summary: Generate Test Cases from Approved Scenarios
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I have one or more approved test scenarios selected, When I trigger the 'Generate Test Cases' action, Then the system should create detailed test cases for each selected scenario.
• Each generated test case should include a unique identifier, clear steps to reproduce, expected results, and a link back to the originating scenario and user story.
• I should be able to review, edit, and save the generated test cases.
• The system should support generating test cases in a structured format suitable for eventual export or automation asset creation.

userStories.description: As a user, I want to create and manage folders within a project so that I can organize my acceptance criteria, scenarios, and test cases hierarchically for better navigation and management.
userStories.summary: Manage Project Folders and Organize Assets
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am within a project, When I click 'Create Folder' and provide a unique name, Then a new folder should be created within the current project or selected parent folder.
• I should be able to drag-and-drop or select items (AC, scenarios, test cases) to move them into different folders.
• I should be able to rename existing folders.
• When I attempt to delete an empty folder, Then it should be removed successfully.
• When I attempt to delete a folder containing assets, Then the system should prompt for confirmation or offer options to move contents before deletion.

userStories.description: As a QA Lead or Product Owner, I want to view reports on test coverage, generation status, and automation assets so that I can monitor project progress, identify areas for improvement, and ensure business objectives are met.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am on the reports dashboard, When I select a specific project, Then I should see summary reports including key metrics such as the count of imported Jira stories, generated acceptance criteria, generated scenarios, and generated test cases.
• The reports should visually represent test coverage against requirements (e.g., how many stories have AC, how many AC have scenarios, etc.).
• I should be able to filter reports by various criteria (e.g., date range, status of items, assigned user).
• The reports should be presented in a clear, concise, and easy-to-understand format (e.g., charts, tables).
• The reports should load within an acceptable time frame (e.g., less than 3 seconds) even for large projects.

scenarios.title: Successful User Login with Valid Credentials
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario validates the core functionality of logging into the AutomatiQA platform using valid, registered credentials. The user, acting as an authenticated user, navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, inputs a correct username and password, and clicks the 'Login' button. This directly covers Acceptance Criterion 1. The 'Global Login Context' implies that pre-configured valid credentials are used for this test.
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should be successfully redirected to the main dashboard of the AutomatiQA platform.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Invalid Username
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the system's response when an incorrect or unregistered username is provided during the login process. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters a valid password but an invalid/unregistered username, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 2.
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Invalid Password
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the system's response when an incorrect password is provided for a valid username during the login process. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters a valid username but an invalid password, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 2.
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.

scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario verifies the system's handling when both the username and password provided are incorrect or unregistered. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters an unregistered username and an incorrect password, and clicks 'Login'. This covers Acceptance Criterion 2.
scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Both Invalid Username and Password
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.
An appropriate validation message (e.g., 'Username is required' or 'Please enter your username') should be displayed below the username field, and the user should remain on the login page.
scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Blank Username Field
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the client-side or server-side validation for the username field when it is left blank. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, leaves the username field empty, enters a valid password, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 3.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Blank Password Field
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the client-side or server-side validation for the password field when it is left blank. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters a valid username, leaves the password field empty, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 3.
scenarios.expectedResults: An appropriate validation message (e.g., 'Password is required' or 'Please enter your password') should be displayed below the password field, and the user should remain on the login page.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Both Username and Password Fields Blank
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the combined validation when both the username and password fields are left blank. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, leaves both fields empty, and clicks 'Login'. This covers Acceptance Criterion 3.
scenarios.expectedResults: Appropriate validation messages for both username and password fields should be displayed, and the user should remain on the login page.

scenarios.title: Login Performance Measurement
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario measures the time taken for a successful login process. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters valid credentials, and clicks 'Login'. The duration from the click event on the 'Login' button to the complete loading and display of the main dashboard is observed. This directly addresses Acceptance Criterion 4.
scenarios.expectedResults: The entire login process, including redirection and dashboard load, should complete within 3 seconds.

scenarios.title: Password Input Masking for Security
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario verifies that the password entered by the user is correctly masked (displayed as asterisks or dots) to prevent shoulder-surfing or accidental disclosure. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page and types characters into the password field.
scenarios.expectedResults: The characters entered in the password field should be masked (e.g., '*****') instead of being visible in plain text. A toggle ('show/hide password') functionality, if present, should also work as expected.

scenarios.title: Brute Force Attack Protection
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario assesses the system's security measures against brute force attacks. The user repeatedly attempts to log in using a valid username but multiple incorrect passwords, or various invalid username/password combinations, within a short period to exceed a typical threshold for failed login attempts.
scenarios.expectedResults: After a predefined number of failed login attempts (e.g., 3-5 times), the system should implement a security measure such as: temporarily locking the user account, presenting a CAPTCHA challenge, or introducing a delay between login attempts. An informative message should be displayed to the user regarding the action taken.

scenarios.title: Login after Session Timeout
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario verifies the system's behavior when a user attempts to re-login after their previous authenticated session has expired due to inactivity. The user first successfully logs in, remains inactive until the server-side session times out, and is then redirected to the login page upon attempting to access any protected resource. The user then proceeds to log in again with valid credentials.
scenarios.expectedResults: Upon re-logging in with valid credentials after a session timeout, the user should be successfully redirected to the main dashboard. The system should correctly invalidate the old session and establish a new, valid session.

For username: If the system expects case-sensitive usernames (common security practice), the login should fail with 'Invalid username or password' for incorrect casing.For password: Login should always fail with 'Invalid username or password' for incorrect password casing, as passwords are universally case-sensitive.
scenarios.title: Case Sensitivity of Username and Password
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the case sensitivity rules applied to the username and password fields during login. The user attempts to log in using: 1. A valid username with incorrect casing (e.g., 'User' instead of 'user', assuming it's meant to be case-sensitive). 2. A valid username with an exact but a valid password with incorrect casing (e.g., 'password123' instead of 'Password123').

testCases.expectedResult: The system automatically identifies the correct patient responsibility (e.g., $50.00 co-pay), sends a detailed email notification to 'John Doe' with the accurate balance and a functional payment portal link, and updates the patient's ledger to 'Awaiting Payment' status.
steps: 1. Setup Pre-condition: Configure a patient record (e.g., 'John Doe') with a completed visit and an insurance claim that processes, resulting in a specific patient co-pay amount (e.g., $50.00) and no other outstanding balances. Ensure 'John Doe' has a valid email address configured.

2. From an administrative interface or via a backend script, update the insurance claim status for 'John Doe' to 'Finalized' or 'Processed & Billed', simulating the trigger for the automated post-claim processing workflow.
3. Monitor system logs or audit trails for the initiation of a payment collection workflow for 'John Doe' following the claim status update.
4. Access the patient's financial ledger or billing summary within the system.
5. Verify that the system accurately displays the patient's outstanding responsibility, which should match the configured co-pay amount (e.g., $50.00).
6. Verify that the outstanding balance is recorded with a status of 'Awaiting Payment' or 'Patient Responsibility - Outstanding' in the ledger.
7. Check the configured outbound email gateway logs or a dedicated email audit feature within the system for a new email sent to 'John Doe's' registered email address.
8. Confirm that the email subject indicates a payment notification (e.g., 'Your Recent Visit - Payment Due').
9. Verify the email content includes the patient's name, the correct balance due (e.g., $50.00), and a clickable, valid link to the payment portal.
10. Verify that the link to the payment portal is functional by attempting to access it (without completing a payment).

scenarios.description: Test the system's ability to identify and initiate collection for a patient designated as 'self-pay', where the entire visit cost is their responsibility.
scenarios.title: Self-Pay Patient Balance Identification and Collection
scenarios.expectedResults: The system correctly identifies 100% of the visit cost as patient responsibility, and initiates the standard collection workflow (e.g., email notification, payment portal link) for the full amount.

scenarios.description: Verify the system accurately calculates patient responsibility when both primary and secondary insurance claims have been processed, ensuring the correct remaining balance is identified.
scenarios.title: Patient with Multiple Insurance Plans - Correct Responsibility Calculation
scenarios.expectedResults: The system processes both primary and secondary insurance claims, calculates the exact remaining patient responsibility, and initiates collection for that amount.
The patient can securely access the payment portal via the provided link, view the correct outstanding balance, and see a breakdown of charges if applicable.
scenarios.description: A patient receives a payment notification, uses the provided link, and successfully accesses the secure payment portal to view their outstanding balance and related details.
scenarios.title: Patient Accesses and Navigates Payment Portal

scenarios.description: After accessing the payment portal, a patient successfully enters valid payment details (e.g., credit card) and submits payment for the identified outstanding balance.
scenarios.title: Patient Submits Successful Payment via Portal
scenarios.expectedResults: The payment is successfully processed through the integrated payment gateway, the patient receives a confirmation, their balance is updated to zero, and the payment is recorded in the system.
The Revenue Cycle Manager can log in successfully and access an accurate, up-to-date report showing all patients with outstanding balances, including details like amount due, visit date, and status.
scenarios.title: Revenue Cycle Manager Views Outstanding Balances Report
scenarios.description: As a Revenue Cycle Manager, log in using Global Login credentials and verify the ability to access and view a report listing all outstanding patient balances.
Verify that a Practice Administrator can manually trigger the payment collection workflow for a specific patient's outstanding balance, overriding automated schedules if needed.
scenarios.title: Manual Trigger of Collection Workflow by Administrator
scenarios.expectedResults: The Practice Administrator successfully initiates a manual collection workflow (e.g., sends a reminder email) for a selected patient, and the system records this manual action.

The system identifies patient responsibilities and initiates collection workflows for all concurrent visits within acceptable performance thresholds (e.g., response times, processing speed) without errors or significant delays.
scenarios.description: Assess the system's performance when simultaneously identifying patient responsibilities for a large number of completed visits (e.g., 1000+) and initiating their respective payment collection workflows.
scenarios.title: System Performance Under High Load (Identification & Workflow)

scenarios.description: Verify that the patient payment portal uses industry-standard encryption protocols (e.g., HTTPS, TLS 1.2+) to protect sensitive patient and payment information during transmission.
scenarios.title: Security of Patient Payment Portal (Data Encryption)
scenarios.expectedResults: All communication between the patient's browser and the payment portal, including submission of payment details, is encrypted, as indicated by security indicators (e.g., padlock icon, valid SSL certificate).

scenarios.title: Scalability of Communication (High Volume Notifications)
scenarios.description: Evaluate the system's ability to efficiently send a high volume of payment notification emails and/or SMS messages (e.g., 5000+ per hour) without degradation in delivery speed or success rate.
scenarios.expectedResults: All scheduled payment notifications are sent within the expected timeframe, and delivery rates remain high, indicating the system's communication infrastructure can scale effectively.
The payment portal is intuitive, clearly displays the amount due, provides simple instructions for payment, and allows a patient to complete a transaction without confusion or difficulty.
scenarios.description: Assess the ease of use, clarity of instructions, and overall user experience of the patient payment portal from a patient's perspective.
scenarios.title: Usability and Clarity of Patient Payment Portal

scenarios.expectedResults: The system correctly identifies zero patient responsibility after insurance processing and does NOT initiate any payment collection emails, SMS, or postal mail.
scenarios.title: Zero Patient Responsibility Identified
scenarios.description: Test a scenario where the patient's insurance fully covers the visit, resulting in zero patient responsibility, and ensure no collection workflow is initiated.

scenarios.expectedResults: The system identifies the credit balance for the patient, does not initiate a collection workflow, and potentially flags the account for a refund process (if supported) or applies the credit to future services.
scenarios.description: Verify the system's behavior when a patient's upfront payment or previous credit exceeds their final determined responsibility, resulting in a credit balance.
scenarios.title: Pre-Payment Exceeds Final Responsibility (Credit Balance)

scenarios.expectedResults: If configured to do so, the system initiates a communication to the patient based on an estimated responsibility while clearly stating the claim is pending and the amount may change. Otherwise, it should wait for final adjudication.
scenarios.description: Determine if the system waits for full insurance adjudication or initiates collection based on an estimated patient responsibility if the insurance claim is still pending after a set timeframe.
scenarios.title: Insurance Claim Pending - Initial Collection Estimate

scenarios.description: Test the scenario where a patient has made a partial payment, but a remaining balance is still due. The system should accurately calculate and collect the outstanding amount.
scenarios.title: Partial Payment Made - Collect Remaining Balance
scenarios.expectedResults: The system identifies the partial payment, calculates the correct remaining balance, and initiates a collection workflow specifically for that remaining amount, clearly communicating the outstanding sum.
The system should reject the payment attempt, display a clear and helpful error message to the patient (e.g., 'Invalid card number', 'Card expired'), and not process the transaction.
scenarios.title: Invalid Payment Information Submission by Patient
scenarios.description: A patient attempts to make a payment through the portal using invalid credit card details (e.g., incorrect number, expired date, wrong CVV).

scenarios.expectedResults: The system should detect the payment gateway issue, display an appropriate error message to the patient (e.g., 'Payment service temporarily unavailable, please try again later'), and ensure no partial or failed transactions are recorded incorrectly.
scenarios.description: Simulate a scenario where the integrated payment gateway is unavailable or experiences an error during a patient's attempt to submit a payment.
scenarios.title: Payment Gateway Downtime During Patient Payment Attempt

scenarios.description: Verify that if a patient has opted out of email/SMS communications, the system respects this preference and uses an alternative collection method (e.g., physical mail) or flags for manual follow-up.
scenarios.title: Patient Opts Out of Digital Communication
scenarios.expectedResults: The system identifies the patient's communication preference, refrains from sending digital notifications, and initiates the designated alternative collection method or alerts an administrator for manual action.

scenarios.title: Failed Email Delivery (Bounced Email)
scenarios.description: Test the system's handling of bounced email notifications due to invalid email addresses or full inboxes.
scenarios.expectedResults: The system should register the email as undeliverable, potentially update the patient's contact status, and trigger an alternative communication method or an alert for administrative review.
The system should deny access to the unauthorized user, display an appropriate permission error message, and log the failed attempt.
scenarios.description: An administrative user without the appropriate roles or permissions attempts to manually trigger or modify a patient's payment collection workflow.
scenarios.title: Unauthorized Access to Payment Workflow Actions

scenarios.expectedResults: The system should either proceed with the standard collection workflow for the small amount or, if configured, automatically waive the balance and record it as a small balance write-off, without initiating collection.
scenarios.title: Collect Extremely Small Balance
scenarios.description: Verify the system's behavior when the identified patient responsibility is a very small amount (e.g., less than $1.00).

## Corrected UI Report

**Application Module:** Online Shop Instructions Modal

This report outlines the corrected UI specification for the "How to Use the Online Shop" modal, addressing all previously identified issues to ensure a clean, professional, and accurate user experience.

---

### Spelling and Grammar Issues Corrected

The following text elements have been updated to reflect correct spelling, grammar, and word usage:

*   **Modal Title:**
    *   **Text:** "How to Use the Online Shop" (No change required, already correct).
*   **Instructional Text (Bullet Points):**
    *   **1. Browse our products and select the items you want to buy.**
        *   **Correction 1:** Changed `product's` to **`products`** (plural).
        *   **Correction 2:** Changed `by` to **`buy`**.
    *   **2. Add your chosen items to the cart and proceed to checkout.**
        *   **Correction 1:** Changed `chossen` to **`chosen`**.
        *   **Correction 2:** Changed `ceckout` to **`checkout`**.
    *   **3. Complete the payment and receive your order confirmation email.**
        *   **Correction 1:** Changed `Compleat` to **`Complete`**.
        *   **Correction 2:** Changed `recive` to **`receive`**.
        *   **Correction 3:** Changed `cofirmation` to **`confirmation`**.
*   **Thank You Message:**
    *   **Text:** "Thank you for shopping with us!" (No change required, already correct).
*   **"OK" Button:**
    *   **Text:** "OK" (No change required, already correct).

### Layout Issues Corrected

*   No UI layout issues were detected in the original analysis. The current layout, including element positioning, spacing, and sizing within the modal, is considered appropriate and aligned with design best practices. All elements remain clearly visible, well-aligned, and provide a balanced visual hierarchy.

### Visual Consistency Summary

The corrected UI maintains strong visual consistency across all elements within the modal and with the broader application design.

*   **Modal Structure:** The modal retains its distinct white background, subtle drop shadow, and a semi-transparent overlay to ensure focus on the instructional content. The header bar with a prominent title and close button remains visually consistent.
*   **Typography:** All text elements (title, bullet points, thank you message, button text) adhere to the application's established font families, sizes, and weights, ensuring readability and a consistent brand appearance.
*   **Interactive Elements:** The "OK" button maintains its grey background, white text, and rounded corners, consistent with other interactive elements within the application. The close "X" icon also maintains its expected appearance and functionality.
*   **Spacing and Alignment:** Consistent internal padding, line spacing, and horizontal alignment of text and button elements contribute to a clean, uncluttered presentation.

This corrected UI specification ensures that the "How to Use the Online Shop" modal provides clear, accurate, and professional guidance to users, enhancing the overall user experience.

requests.expectedResults: The API should respond with a 400 Bad Request status code and an appropriate error message indicating that 'userId' is a required field.

As a registered user, I want to securely log in to the AutomatiQA platform so that I can access its features and manage my testing assets.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am on the login page, When I enter valid credentials and click 'Login', Then I should be authenticated and redirected to the project dashboard.
• Given I am on the login page, When I enter invalid credentials and click 'Login', Then I should see an error message indicating invalid credentials.
• Given I am on the login page, When I leave required fields (e.g., username, password) empty and click 'Login', Then I should see validation errors for the empty fields.
• Given I am logged in, When my session expires or I log out, Then I should be prompted to log in again to access the system.
• The login process must use secure protocols (e.g., HTTPS) and protect user credentials.

userStories.description: As a user with appropriate permissions, I want to create a new project within AutomatiQA so that I can organize my test automation efforts for a specific application or product.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am on the project management page and have 'Create Project' permissions, When I click 'Create New Project', enter a unique project name and description, and click 'Save', Then the new project should be created successfully and appear in my project list.
• Given I am on the project management page, When I attempt to create a project with a name that already exists, Then I should receive an error message indicating that project names must be unique.
• Given I am on the project management page, When I attempt to create a project with an empty project name, Then I should receive a validation error.
• Only users with the 'Project Creator' role (or similar) should be able to create new projects.

• Given I am logged in and navigate to the project selection screen, Then I should see a list of all projects that have been assigned to me.
• Each project in the list should display its name and a brief description.
• I should not be able to see or access projects to which I have not been explicitly assigned.
• Clicking on a project in the list should navigate me to that project's dashboard or overview.
userStories.description: As a registered user, I want to view a list of projects I have access to so that I can select and work on a specific project.

userStories.summary: Configure Jira Integration for a Project
userStories.description: As a project administrator, I want to configure the integration with Jira for a specific project so that AutomatiQA can access and import user stories from Jira.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am in a specific project's settings and have 'Admin' permissions, When I provide valid Jira URL, API token/credentials, and the Jira Project Key, Then the integration should be successfully established and verified.
• Given the integration is configured, When I attempt to import Jira stories, Then the system should use the stored configuration and credentials to connect to Jira.
• If invalid Jira credentials or an inaccessible Jira instance is provided, Then an appropriate error message should be displayed, and the integration should not be saved.

userStories.description: As a user, I want to import user stories from a connected Jira project so that I can use them as a basis for generating acceptance criteria and test scenarios.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given Jira integration is successfully configured for my current project, When I initiate the 'Import Jira Stories' action, Then a list of available user stories from the connected Jira project should be displayed.
• Given I have selected specific Jira user stories from the displayed list, When I confirm the import, Then these stories should be imported into AutomatiQA, retaining their original Jira IDs and key details (e.g., summary, description).
• Each imported story in AutomatiQA should have a clear link or reference back to its corresponding Jira issue.
• The system should handle cases where a Jira story has already been imported, preventing duplicates or offering update options.

userStories.description: As a QA Lead or Business Analyst, I want to use AI to generate comprehensive acceptance criteria for an imported Jira user story so that I can quickly define clear expectations for testing.
userStories.summary: Generate AI-Powered Acceptance Criteria for a User Story
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I have selected an imported Jira user story, When I trigger the 'Generate Acceptance Criteria' action, Then the AI model should process the story's description and propose a set of acceptance criteria.
• The generated acceptance criteria should be displayed in a review interface, allowing me to accept, modify, or reject individual criteria.
• I should be able to manually add, edit, or delete acceptance criteria even after AI generation.
• When I finalize the criteria, Then they should be saved and permanently associated with the selected user story.
• The AI generation process should complete within an acceptable time frame (e.g., less than 3 seconds).

• Given I have a user story with finalized acceptance criteria, When I trigger the 'Generate AI Scenarios' action, Then the AI model should propose multiple, distinct test scenarios that cover all associated acceptance criteria.
• The generated scenarios should be displayed for review, allowing me to select, modify, or deselect them.
• I should be able to save the selected AI-generated scenarios, ensuring they are associated with the originating user story and its acceptance criteria.
• Each generated scenario should clearly outline a sequence of steps and an expected outcome.
• The system should ensure that AI-generated scenarios are saved in association with their respective user stories as per business rules.
userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to use AI to generate detailed test scenarios based on a user story and its acceptance criteria so that I can efficiently plan my testing efforts.
userStories.summary: Generate AI-Powered Test Scenarios from User Stories and Acceptance Criteria

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to generate concrete test cases from the approved test scenarios so that I can create executable tests for automation or manual execution.
userStories.summary: Generate Test Cases from Approved Scenarios
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I have one or more approved test scenarios selected, When I trigger the 'Generate Test Cases' action, Then the system should create detailed test cases for each selected scenario.
• Each generated test case should include a unique identifier, clear steps to reproduce, expected results, and a link back to the originating scenario and user story.
• I should be able to review, edit, and save the generated test cases.
• The system should support generating test cases in a structured format suitable for eventual export or automation asset creation.

userStories.description: As a user, I want to create and manage folders within a project so that I can organize my acceptance criteria, scenarios, and test cases hierarchically for better navigation and management.
userStories.summary: Manage Project Folders and Organize Assets
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am within a project, When I click 'Create Folder' and provide a unique name, Then a new folder should be created within the current project or selected parent folder.
• I should be able to drag-and-drop or select items (AC, scenarios, test cases) to move them into different folders.
• I should be able to rename existing folders.
• When I attempt to delete an empty folder, Then it should be removed successfully.
• When I attempt to delete a folder containing assets, Then the system should prompt for confirmation or offer options to move contents before deletion.

userStories.description: As a QA Lead or Product Owner, I want to view reports on test coverage, generation status, and automation assets so that I can monitor project progress, identify areas for improvement, and ensure business objectives are met.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• Given I am on the reports dashboard, When I select a specific project, Then I should see summary reports including key metrics such as the count of imported Jira stories, generated acceptance criteria, generated scenarios, and generated test cases.
• The reports should visually represent test coverage against requirements (e.g., how many stories have AC, how many AC have scenarios, etc.).
• I should be able to filter reports by various criteria (e.g., date range, status of items, assigned user).
• The reports should be presented in a clear, concise, and easy-to-understand format (e.g., charts, tables).
• The reports should load within an acceptable time frame (e.g., less than 3 seconds) even for large projects.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I am in a project, when I navigate to the 'Reports' section, then I should see a dashboard or report showing key metrics.Given the report is displayed, then it should include metrics such as total user stories imported, number of stories with generated acceptance criteria, number of stories with generated scenarios, and total number of test cases.Given the report is displayed, then the data presented should be up-to-date with the latest activities and asset creations/updates within the project.Given I can click on a metric (e.g., 'Stories with AC'), then it should navigate me to a filtered view showing those specific stories.

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to export generated test cases and scenarios so that I can use them in external tools or share them with stakeholders.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I have generated test cases/scenarios, when I select them and click 'Export', then I should be prompted to choose an export format (e.g., CSV, Excel, JSON).Given I select an export format (e.g., CSV), then the selected test cases/scenarios should be downloaded in the chosen format, containing all relevant details (summary, steps, expected results, associated story ID).Given my project is connected to Jira, when I select test cases for export, then an option should be available to push them back to Jira as test cases/issues, if supported by Jira's API or a connected plugin.Given an export fails (e.g., due to large file size, network issue), then an informative error message should be displayed.

userStories.description: As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I am on the AutomatiQA login page, When I enter valid credentials (username and password) and click 'Login', Then I should be successfully redirected to the main dashboard.Given I am on the AutomatiQA login page, When I enter invalid credentials and click 'Login', Then I should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.Given I am on the AutomatiQA login page, When I leave either the username or password field blank and click 'Login', Then I should see appropriate validation messages indicating required fields.Given I am on the AutomatiQA login page, When I successfully log in, Then the login process should complete within 3 seconds.

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to create new projects and manage existing ones within AutomatiQA, so that I can organize and compartmentalize testing efforts for different initiatives.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I am logged in and navigate to the Project Management section, When I click 'Create New Project', Then I should be presented with a form to enter project details including Project Name and Description.When I submit the 'Create New Project' form with a unique project name and valid details, Then the new project should be successfully created and added to my list of accessible projects.When I attempt to create a project with a name that already exists within the system, Then I should receive an error message 'Project name already exists' and the project should not be created.Given I have created or have access to projects, When I view the Project Management section, Then I should see a list of all projects I am assigned to, displaying their names and descriptions.When I select an existing project from the list, Then I should be navigated to the dashboard specific to that project.

userStories.summary: Configure Jira Integration for a Project
userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to configure the integration between an AutomatiQA project and a specific Jira instance, so that I can import requirements and link test assets.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I have selected an AutomatiQA project, When I navigate to the 'Jira Integration' settings, Then I should be able to input the Jira URL, a valid API token or username/password.When I provide valid Jira configuration details and click 'Connect', Then the system should establish a successful connection to Jira and display a confirmation message.When I provide invalid Jira configuration details or the Jira instance is unreachable, Then the system should display an appropriate error message indicating connection failure.Given Jira is connected, When I save the configuration, Then the system should securely store the credentials and settings for future use within this project.

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to import user stories from a connected Jira project into AutomatiQA, so that I can use them as the basis for AI-powered test generation.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given an AutomatiQA project is successfully integrated with a Jira instance, When I navigate to the 'Import Jira Stories' section, Then I should be able to select a Jira project and filter by issue types (e.g., Story, Epic).When I select specific Jira user stories and initiate the import, Then these user stories should be imported into the AutomatiQA project, preserving their original ID, Summary, Description, and other relevant fields.Then each imported story should maintain a traceable link back to its corresponding Jira ticket.When the Jira service is unavailable or network latency is high during import, Then the system should provide clear feedback to the user about the issue and handle potential partial imports gracefully.

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to leverage AI to generate acceptance criteria for an imported Jira user story, so that I can quickly and comprehensively define the expected behavior.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I have an imported Jira user story selected, When I initiate the 'Generate Acceptance Criteria' action, Then the AI service should process the user story's description and generate a list of acceptance criteria.Then the generated acceptance criteria should be displayed in a clear, editable format (e.g., Gherkin-like Given-When-Then format).I should be able to review, modify, add, or delete individual acceptance criteria before saving them.When I save the acceptance criteria, Then they should be associated with the selected Jira user story.Given the AI service is temporarily unavailable or returns poor output, Then I should still be able to manually define and save acceptance criteria for the story.

userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to generate AI-powered test scenarios based on defined acceptance criteria, so that I can broaden my test coverage and identify various use cases and edge cases.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I have an imported Jira story with defined acceptance criteria, When I initiate the 'Generate AI Scenarios' action, Then the AI service should process the acceptance criteria and generate a set of test scenarios.Then the generated scenarios should be displayed in a readable, editable format, outlining different paths and conditions.I should be able to review, modify, add, or delete individual scenarios before saving them.When I save the scenarios, Then they must be linked to the associated user story and its acceptance criteria.Given the AI service is temporarily unavailable or returns poor output, Then I should still be able to manually define and save scenarios for the story.

userStories.summary: Generate Detailed Test Cases from Scenarios
userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to generate detailed test cases from approved test scenarios, so that I have actionable, step-by-step instructions for manual or automated testing.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I have a set of approved test scenarios for a user story, When I select the 'Generate Test Cases' option, Then the system should generate detailed test cases for each scenario.Then each generated test case should include a unique identifier, clear steps, expected results, and any necessary pre-conditions.I should be able to review, modify, and save the generated test cases.Then generated test cases should be clearly linked to their respective scenarios and the parent user story, ensuring traceability.When I modify a scenario, Then the system should prompt me to review and potentially update its associated test cases.

userStories.summary: Organize Test Assets with Folder Management
userStories.description: As a Test Engineer, I want to create and manage folders, so that I can logically organize acceptance criteria, scenarios, and test cases within a project.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I am within an AutomatiQA project, When I navigate to the asset management area, Then I should be able to create new folders and subfolders.I should be able to drag-and-drop or use a context menu to move existing acceptance criteria, scenarios, and test cases into specific folders.I should be able to rename existing folders.When I attempt to delete a folder containing assets, Then the system should provide a warning about deleting its contents and offer options to reassign or permanently delete the assets.Then all saved acceptance criteria, scenarios, and test cases must be assignable to a specific folder for structured organization.

userStories.summary: View Comprehensive Test Coverage and Progress Reports
userStories.description: As a QA Lead, I want to view comprehensive reports on test coverage and progress, so that I can assess the completeness of testing for a project and identify any gaps or areas needing attention.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I am logged in and have selected a project, When I navigate to the 'Reports' section, Then I should see options to generate various reports, including 'Test Coverage' and 'Test Progress'.When I generate a 'Test Coverage' report, Then it should display key metrics such as the number of user stories with acceptance criteria, the number of scenarios generated per story, and the number of test cases created per scenario.The reports should visually represent the linkage and traceability between requirements, acceptance criteria, scenarios, and test cases.When I generate a 'Test Progress' report, Then it should display the status of test case execution (e.g., Passed, Failed, Blocked) and provide insights into overall testing completeness.

userStories.summary: Export Generated Test Assets and Reports
userStories.description: As a QA Lead or Test Engineer, I want to export generated test cases and reports, so that I can utilize them in other testing tools, share them with stakeholders, or maintain offline records.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given I have generated test cases or reports, When I select an export option, Then I should be presented with a choice of common export formats (e.g., CSV, Excel, JSON).When I select a format and initiate the export, Then the system should generate a file containing the selected data, accurately reflecting its content and structure.Then the exported file should be downloadable to my local system.The export process should be efficient, even for large sets of data.When exporting test cases, Then relevant details such as steps, expected results, associated story, and scenario should be included.

scenarios.title: Successful User Login with Valid Credentials
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario validates the core functionality of logging into the AutomatiQA platform using valid, registered credentials. The user, acting as an authenticated user, navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, inputs a correct username and password, and clicks the 'Login' button. This directly covers Acceptance Criterion 1. The 'Global Login Context' implies that pre-configured valid credentials are used for this test.
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should be successfully redirected to the main dashboard of the AutomatiQA platform.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Invalid Username
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the system's response when an incorrect or unregistered username is provided during the login process. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters a valid password but an invalid/unregistered username, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 2.
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Invalid Password
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the system's response when an incorrect password is provided for a valid username during the login process. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters a valid username but an invalid password, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 2.
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.

scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario verifies the system's handling when both the username and password provided are incorrect or unregistered. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters an unregistered username and an incorrect password, and clicks 'Login'. This covers Acceptance Criterion 2.
scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Both Invalid Username and Password
scenarios.expectedResults: The user should receive an error message 'Invalid username or password' and remain on the login page.
An appropriate validation message (e.g., 'Username is required' or 'Please enter your username') should be displayed below the username field, and the user should remain on the login page.
scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Blank Username Field
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the client-side or server-side validation for the username field when it is left blank. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, leaves the username field empty, enters a valid password, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 3.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Blank Password Field
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the client-side or server-side validation for the password field when it is left blank. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters a valid username, leaves the password field empty, and clicks 'Login'. This covers part of Acceptance Criterion 3.
scenarios.expectedResults: An appropriate validation message (e.g., 'Password is required' or 'Please enter your password') should be displayed below the password field, and the user should remain on the login page.

scenarios.title: Login Attempt with Both Username and Password Fields Blank
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the combined validation when both the username and password fields are left blank. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, leaves both fields empty, and clicks 'Login'. This covers Acceptance Criterion 3.
scenarios.expectedResults: Appropriate validation messages for both username and password fields should be displayed, and the user should remain on the login page.

scenarios.title: Login Performance Measurement
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario measures the time taken for a successful login process. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page, enters valid credentials, and clicks 'Login'. The duration from the click event on the 'Login' button to the complete loading and display of the main dashboard is observed. This directly addresses Acceptance Criterion 4.
scenarios.expectedResults: The entire login process, including redirection and dashboard load, should complete within 3 seconds.

scenarios.title: Password Input Masking for Security
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario verifies that the password entered by the user is correctly masked (displayed as asterisks or dots) to prevent shoulder-surfing or accidental disclosure. The user navigates to the AutomatiQA login page and types characters into the password field.
scenarios.expectedResults: The characters entered in the password field should be masked (e.g., '*****') instead of being visible in plain text. A toggle ('show/hide password') functionality, if present, should also work as expected.

scenarios.title: Brute Force Attack Protection
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario assesses the system's security measures against brute force attacks. The user repeatedly attempts to log in using a valid username but multiple incorrect passwords, or various invalid username/password combinations, within a short period to exceed a typical threshold for failed login attempts.
scenarios.expectedResults: After a predefined number of failed login attempts (e.g., 3-5 times), the system should implement a security measure such as: temporarily locking the user account, presenting a CAPTCHA challenge, or introducing a delay between login attempts. An informative message should be displayed to the user regarding the action taken.

scenarios.title: Login after Session Timeout
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario verifies the system's behavior when a user attempts to re-login after their previous authenticated session has expired due to inactivity. The user first successfully logs in, remains inactive until the server-side session times out, and is then redirected to the login page upon attempting to access any protected resource. The user then proceeds to log in again with valid credentials.
scenarios.expectedResults: Upon re-logging in with valid credentials after a session timeout, the user should be successfully redirected to the main dashboard. The system should correctly invalidate the old session and establish a new, valid session.

For username: If the system expects case-sensitive usernames (common security practice), the login should fail with 'Invalid username or password' for incorrect casing.For password: Login should always fail with 'Invalid username or password' for incorrect password casing, as passwords are universally case-sensitive.
scenarios.title: Case Sensitivity of Username and Password
scenarios.description: **User Story Number:** US-001**User Story Description:** As an authenticated user, I want to log in to the AutomatiQA platform, so that I can access its features and manage test automation assets.---This scenario tests the case sensitivity rules applied to the username and password fields during login. The user attempts to log in using: 1. A valid username with incorrect casing (e.g., 'User' instead of 'user', assuming it's meant to be case-sensitive). 2. A valid username with an exact but a valid password with incorrect casing (e.g., 'password123' instead of 'Password123').

testCases.expectedResult: The system automatically identifies the correct patient responsibility (e.g., $50.00 co-pay), sends a detailed email notification to 'John Doe' with the accurate balance and a functional payment portal link, and updates the patient's ledger to 'Awaiting Payment' status.
steps: 1. Setup Pre-condition: Configure a patient record (e.g., 'John Doe') with a completed visit and an insurance claim that processes, resulting in a specific patient co-pay amount (e.g., $50.00) and no other outstanding balances. Ensure 'John Doe' has a valid email address configured.

2. From an administrative interface or via a backend script, update the insurance claim status for 'John Doe' to 'Finalized' or 'Processed & Billed', simulating the trigger for the automated post-claim processing workflow.
3. Monitor system logs or audit trails for the initiation of a payment collection workflow for 'John Doe' following the claim status update.
4. Access the patient's financial ledger or billing summary within the system.
5. Verify that the system accurately displays the patient's outstanding responsibility, which should match the configured co-pay amount (e.g., $50.00).
6. Verify that the outstanding balance is recorded with a status of 'Awaiting Payment' or 'Patient Responsibility - Outstanding' in the ledger.
7. Check the configured outbound email gateway logs or a dedicated email audit feature within the system for a new email sent to 'John Doe's' registered email address.
8. Confirm that the email subject indicates a payment notification (e.g., 'Your Recent Visit - Payment Due').
9. Verify the email content includes the patient's name, the correct balance due (e.g., $50.00), and a clickable, valid link to the payment portal.
10. Verify that the link to the payment portal is functional by attempting to access it (without completing a payment).
testCases.title: Verify successful automatic identification of patient responsibility and email notification for standard co-pay.
testDataSets: Patient Name: John Doe, Patient ID: P-001, Visit ID: V-101, Co-pay: $50.00, Deductible: $0.00, Total Responsibility: $50.00, Patient Email: john.doe@example.com, Payment Portal Link: https://payment.example.com/portal/P-001

Patient Name: Jane Smith, Patient ID: P-002, Visit ID: V-102, Co-pay: $0.00, Deductible: $150.00, Total Responsibility: $150.00, Patient Email: jane.smith@example.com, Payment Portal Link: https://payment.example.com/portal/P-002

Patient Name: Alex Johnson, Patient ID: P-003, Visit ID: V-103, Co-pay: $25.00, Deductible: $75.00, Total Responsibility: $100.00, Patient Email: alex.johnson@example.com, Payment Portal Link: https://payment.example.com/portal/P-003

steps: Precondition: Ensure the patient account is active and configured for "Global Login Context". (This step implies that the authentication part of the login is handled by the system, bypassing manual entry and OTP.)
Navigate to the base URL of the Patient Portal application.
Verify that the application successfully authenticates the patient through the "Global Login Context" and lands on the Patient Dashboard or Home screen.
Locate and click on the "Find a Doctor" or "View Providers" option/link, typically found in the main navigation or dashboard quick links.
Observe the page content to ensure a list of doctors/providers is displayed.

For each displayed doctor, verify the presence of the Doctor's Name, Specialty (e.g., "Cardiology", "Pediatrics"), and Basic Availability Status (e.g., "Available Today", "Next slot in 3 days", "Book Now").
Verify that the list is populated with multiple distinct doctor entries and is not empty.
If the list is extensive, check for any pagination, infinite scroll functionality, or filters, confirming that more doctors can be viewed or refined.
testCases.expectedResult: The patient is successfully authenticated and logged into the application, landing on the Patient Dashboard. Upon navigating to the doctor list, a detailed and comprehensive list of doctors/providers is presented, clearly showing their names, specialties, and current availability for appointment scheduling.
testCases.title: Verify patient successfully logs in via Global Login and views a comprehensive doctor list
testDataSets: Global Login Context: Active Patient User, Doctor List Data: Diverse specialties, mixed availability (some immediate, some later).
Global Login Context: Active Patient User, Doctor List Data: Limited specialists (e.g., only General Practitioners), full availability across all.
Global Login Context: Active Patient User, Doctor List Data: Extensive list (50+ entries), requiring pagination/scrolling, various specialties and availability statuses.

requests.name: Indihood

requests.description: Send a GET request to the /posts endpoint without any parameters.
requests.name: Verify successful retrieval of all posts
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 200 OK status code and a JSON array containing a list of post objects.
The response body should be a valid JSON array.
requests.name: Validate response body structure
requests.description: After a successful GET request to /posts, check if the response is a JSON array.

requests.name: Validate schema of individual post objects
requests.description: For each object in the response array, verify it contains 'id', 'userId', 'title', and 'body' fields.
requests.expectedResults: Each post object must contain the fields 'id', 'userId', 'title', and 'body'.
The 'id' and 'userId' fields should be integers, and 'title' and 'body' fields should be strings.
requests.name: Verify data types for post object fields
requests.description: For each post object, validate the data types of 'id', 'userId', 'title', and 'body'.
Check if all 'id' values in the response array are unique and in sequential order.
requests.name: Verify 'id' fields are unique and sequential
requests.expectedResults: The 'id' field should be unique for each post object and appear in sequential ascending order (1, 2, 3, ...).
The 'title' field of every post object should contain a non-empty string.
requests.name: Verify 'title' field is not empty
requests.description: For each post object, check if the 'title' string is not empty or null.

requests.expectedResults: The 'body' field of every post object should contain a non-empty string.
requests.description: For each post object, check if the 'body' string is not empty or null.
requests.name: Verify 'body' field is not empty

requests.expectedResults: The response array should contain exactly 100 post objects.
requests.description: After a successful GET request to /posts, count the number of objects in the JSON array.
requests.name: Verify total number of posts returned

requests.expectedResults: Posts should be distributed among various users, typically 10 posts per userId (from 1 to 10) as observed in the sample response.
requests.name: Verify 'userId' distribution
requests.description: Examine the 'userId' values across the returned posts.

requests.name: Verify response headers for standard information
requests.description: After a successful GET request, check for relevant response headers.
requests.expectedResults: The response should include standard headers like 'Content-Type' (e.g., application/json; charset=utf-8) and 'Content-Length'.

requests.name: Successful Cart Creation with Valid Data
requests.description: Verify that a new cart can be successfully created by sending valid userId, date, and product details in the request body.
requests.expectedResults: A new cart object should be returned with a unique 'id' and the submitted 'userId', 'date', and 'products' data, along with a 2xx HTTP status code (e.g., 201 Created).

requests.name: Cart Creation with Multiple Products and Quantities
requests.description: Test creating a cart containing multiple distinct products, each with a specified quantity.
requests.expectedResults: The API should successfully create the cart, and the response should include all submitted product items with their respective quantities, returning a 2xx status code.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Empty Products Array
requests.description: Verify the system's behavior when attempting to create a cart with an empty 'products' array.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either successfully create a cart with an empty products array or return a 4xx status code with an appropriate error message indicating that products are required.

requests.name: Missing Required Field: userId
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart without including the 'userId' field in the request body.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) and an error message indicating that 'userId' is a required field.

requests.name: Invalid Data Type: userId as String
requests.description: Submit a request where 'userId' is provided as a non-integer value (e.g., a string or boolean).
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) with a clear error message about the invalid data type for 'userId'.

requests.name: Invalid Data Format: date as malformed string
requests.description: Submit a request where 'date' is provided in an invalid or unrecognized format (e.g., 'not-a-date', '02/01/26').
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating an invalid date format.

requests.name: Invalid Value: Negative Product Quantity
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart where one of the product quantities is a negative number.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating that quantity must be a positive integer.

requests.name: Invalid Value: Non-existent UserId
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart with a 'userId' that does not correspond to any existing user in the system.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request) indicating that the 'userId' is invalid or not found.

requests.name: Invalid Value: Non-existent ProductId
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart with a 'productId' that does not correspond to any existing product in the system.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request) indicating that one or more 'productId' values are invalid or not found.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Past Date
requests.description: Test creating a cart with a 'date' field set to a past value.
requests.expectedResults: The API should successfully create the cart with the specified past date, returning a 2xx status code.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Extra/Unknown Fields
requests.description: Submit a request body that includes additional, undefined fields not part of the API schema.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either ignore the extra fields and successfully create the cart with a 2xx status code, or return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating unrecognized fields.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Empty Request Body
requests.description: Send a POST request to create a cart with an entirely empty JSON request body.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating missing required fields.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Zero Quantity
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart where one of the product quantities is zero.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating quantity must be a positive integer, or successfully create the cart by omitting the product with zero quantity.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Duplicate Product IDs
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart where the 'products' array contains duplicate entries for the same 'productId'.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either combine the quantities for duplicate products, return a 4xx HTTP status code for invalid input, or treat them as separate line items.
