uiTestingReports.correctedReport:
## Corrected UI Specification

This report details the intended user interface specifications for the "How to Use the Online Shop" modal, incorporating all necessary corrections identified in the UI Testing Report. The goal is to present a clear, grammatically correct, and visually consistent user experience for guiding customers.

### Spelling and Grammar Issues Corrected

The following text elements within the modal have been updated to reflect correct spelling, grammar, and punctuation, ensuring clarity and professionalism:

*   **Bullet Point 1:**
    *   **Corrected Text:** "1. Browse our products and select the items your want to buy."
    *   **Corrections Applied:** The incorrect possessive `product's` has been changed to the plural `products`. The misspelling `by` has been corrected to `buy`.

*   **Bullet Point 2:**
    *   **Corrected Text:** "2. Add your chosen items to the cart and proceed to checkout."
    *   **Corrections Applied:** The misspelling `chossen` has been corrected to `chosen`. The misspelling `ceckout` has been corrected to `checkout`.

*   **Bullet Point 3:**
    *   **Corrected Text:** "3. Complete the payment and receive your order confirmation email."
    *   **Corrections Applied:** The misspelling `Compleat` has been corrected to `Complete`. The misspelling `recive` has been corrected to `receive`. The misspelling `cofirmation` has been corrected to `confirmation`.

*   **Other Text Elements:** The modal title "How to Use the Online Shop", the closing message "Thank you for shopping with us!", and the "OK" button label remain unchanged as no issues were identified for these elements.

### Layout Issues Corrected

No layout issues were identified in the original UI Testing Report. The existing layout of the "How to Use the Online Shop" modal is considered optimal. All elements are appropriately spaced, aligned, and sized, contributing to a clean and organized presentation. The modal is centrally positioned on the screen, maintaining clear focus on its instructional content.

### Visual Consistency Summary

The "How to Use the Online Shop" modal exhibits strong visual consistency, adhering to established UI/UX principles and the application's overall design language.

*   **Header:** The blue header bar with the bold, white title text and the clear 'X' close icon maintains a professional and functional appearance, consistent with common modal designs.
*   **Content Presentation:** The use of a white background for the instructional text ensures high readability. The bulleted list effectively breaks down information into digestible steps.
*   **Action Button:** The "OK" button is centrally located at the bottom of the modal, styled with a distinct gray background and white text, providing a clear and accessible call to action for the user to dismiss the instructions.
*   **Overall Aesthetics:** The modal's design is clean, uncluttered, and intuitive, facilitating a positive user experience by providing essential guidance in a user-friendly format.

requests.name: Indihood

requests.description: Send a GET request to the /posts endpoint without any parameters.
requests.name: Verify successful retrieval of all posts
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 200 OK status code and a JSON array containing a list of post objects.
The response body should be a valid JSON array.
requests.name: Validate response body structure
requests.description: After a successful GET request to /posts, check if the response is a JSON array.

requests.name: Validate schema of individual post objects
requests.description: For each object in the response array, verify it contains 'id', 'userId', 'title', and 'body' fields.
requests.expectedResults: Each post object must contain the fields 'id', 'userId', 'title', and 'body'.
The 'id' and 'userId' fields should be integers, and 'title' and 'body' fields should be strings.
requests.name: Verify data types for post object fields
requests.description: For each post object, validate the data types of 'id', 'userId', 'title', and 'body'.
Check if all 'id' values in the response array are unique and in sequential order.
requests.name: Verify 'id' fields are unique and sequential
requests.expectedResults: The 'id' field should be unique for each post object and appear in sequential ascending order (1, 2, 3, ...).
The 'title' field of every post object should contain a non-empty string.
requests.name: Verify 'title' field is not empty
requests.description: For each post object, check if the 'title' string is not empty or null.

requests.expectedResults: The 'body' field of every post object should contain a non-empty string.
requests.description: For each post object, check if the 'body' string is not empty or null.
requests.name: Verify 'body' field is not empty

requests.expectedResults: The response array should contain exactly 100 post objects.
requests.description: After a successful GET request to /posts, count the number of objects in the JSON array.
requests.name: Verify total number of posts returned

requests.expectedResults: Posts should be distributed among various users, typically 10 posts per userId (from 1 to 10) as observed in the sample response.
requests.name: Verify 'userId' distribution
requests.description: Examine the 'userId' values across the returned posts.

requests.name: Verify response headers for standard information
requests.description: After a successful GET request, check for relevant response headers.
requests.expectedResults: The response should include standard headers like 'Content-Type' (e.g., application/json; charset=utf-8) and 'Content-Length'.

requests.name: Successful Cart Creation with Valid Data
requests.description: Verify that a new cart can be successfully created by sending valid userId, date, and product details in the request body.
requests.expectedResults: A new cart object should be returned with a unique 'id' and the submitted 'userId', 'date', and 'products' data, along with a 2xx HTTP status code (e.g., 201 Created).

requests.name: Cart Creation with Multiple Products and Quantities
requests.description: Test creating a cart containing multiple distinct products, each with a specified quantity.
requests.expectedResults: The API should successfully create the cart, and the response should include all submitted product items with their respective quantities, returning a 2xx status code.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Empty Products Array
requests.description: Verify the system's behavior when attempting to create a cart with an empty 'products' array.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either successfully create a cart with an empty products array or return a 4xx status code with an appropriate error message indicating that products are required.

requests.name: Missing Required Field: userId
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart without including the 'userId' field in the request body.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) and an error message indicating that 'userId' is a required field.

requests.name: Invalid Data Type: userId as String
requests.description: Submit a request where 'userId' is provided as a non-integer value (e.g., a string or boolean).
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) with a clear error message about the invalid data type for 'userId'.

requests.name: Invalid Data Format: date as malformed string
requests.description: Submit a request where 'date' is provided in an invalid or unrecognized format (e.g., 'not-a-date', '02/01/26').
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating an invalid date format.

requests.name: Invalid Value: Negative Product Quantity
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart where one of the product quantities is a negative number.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating that quantity must be a positive integer.

requests.name: Invalid Value: Non-existent UserId
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart with a 'userId' that does not correspond to any existing user in the system.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request) indicating that the 'userId' is invalid or not found.

requests.name: Invalid Value: Non-existent ProductId
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart with a 'productId' that does not correspond to any existing product in the system.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 404 Not Found or 400 Bad Request) indicating that one or more 'productId' values are invalid or not found.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Past Date
requests.description: Test creating a cart with a 'date' field set to a past value.
requests.expectedResults: The API should successfully create the cart with the specified past date, returning a 2xx status code.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Extra/Unknown Fields
requests.description: Submit a request body that includes additional, undefined fields not part of the API schema.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either ignore the extra fields and successfully create the cart with a 2xx status code, or return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating unrecognized fields.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Empty Request Body
requests.description: Send a POST request to create a cart with an entirely empty JSON request body.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating missing required fields.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Zero Quantity
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart where one of the product quantities is zero.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either return a 4xx HTTP status code (e.g., 400 Bad Request) indicating quantity must be a positive integer, or successfully create the cart by omitting the product with zero quantity.

requests.name: Cart Creation with Duplicate Product IDs
requests.description: Attempt to create a cart where the 'products' array contains duplicate entries for the same 'productId'.
requests.expectedResults: The API should either combine the quantities for duplicate products, return a 4xx HTTP status code for invalid input, or treat them as separate line items.

# Corrected UI Specification Report

**Project:** Online Shop Onboarding Modal  
**Status:** Verification Ready (All Issues Resolved)  
**Role:** Lead UI/UX QA Tester  

---

## 1. Corrected Copy (Spelling & Grammar)

The onboarding modal copy has been fully proofread and corrected to ensure professional, error-free communication. Below is the approved copy specification for development.

### First Instruction Text
* **Original Copy:** `1. Browse our product's and select the items your want to by.`
* **Corrected Copy:** `1. Browse our products and select the items you want to buy.`
* **Corrections Implemented:**
  * Removed incorrect apostrophe from **products** (changed from plural possessive to simple plural).
  * Changed the pronoun **your** to **you** to correct the grammar.
  * Corrected homophone spelling of **buy** (changed from *by*).

### Second Instruction Text
* **Original Copy:** `2. Add your chossen items to the cart and proceed to ceckout.`
* **Corrected Copy:** `2. Add your chosen items to the cart and proceed to checkout.`
* **Corrections Implemented:**
  * Corrected misspelling of **chosen** (changed from *chossen*).
  * Corrected misspelling of **checkout** (changed from *ceckout*).

### Third Instruction Text
* **Original Copy:** `3. Compleat the payment and recive your order cofirmation email.`
* **Corrected Copy:** `3. Complete the payment and receive your order confirmation email.`
* **Corrections Implemented:**
  * Corrected misspelling of **Complete** (changed from *Compleat*).
  * Corrected misspelling of **receive** (changed from *recive*).
  * Corrected misspelling of **confirmation** (changed from *cofirmation*).

---

## 2. Visual & Layout Specifications

### Layout Integrity
* **Status:** Verified (No Issues)
* **Specification:** 
  * The vertical alignment and spacing of the bulleted instruction list must remain perfectly centered within the white content container.
  * Padding around the list container must maintain a minimum of `24px` on the left and right borders to prevent text clipping across various screen sizes.
  * The header banner background color (`#2160C4` or equivalent brand blue) must remain visually consistent with the rest of the application's primary branding.

### Button & Navigation Controls
* **Primary Action (OK Button):** Centered horizontally at the bottom of the modal card with equal margin spacing above and below.
* **Dismiss Action (X Button):** Positioned in the top-right corner of the blue header bar, maintaining balanced padding from the top and right margins.

---

## 3. Visual Consistency Summary

| UI Element | Property | Verified / Approved State |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Header Text** | Font / Content | `"How to Use the Online Shop"` (Semibold, White, Centered) |
| **Instruction List** | Typography | Regular weight, dark slate body color, standard line height (`1.5`) for optimal readability. |
| **Footer Action** | Button Style | Rounded corners, medium gray fill with bold white `"OK"` text. |
| **Background Overlay** | Dimming | Standard `0.5` opacity dark overlay behind the modal to focus user attention. |

uiTestingReports.correctedReport:
# Corrected UI Specification Report

**Project:** Online Shop Onboarding Modal  
**Status:** Verification Ready (All Issues Resolved)  
**Role:** Lead UI/UX QA Tester  

---

## 1. Corrected Copy (Spelling & Grammar)

The onboarding modal copy has been fully proofread and corrected to ensure professional, error-free communication. Below is the approved copy specification for development.

### First Instruction Text
* **Original Copy:** `1. Browse our product's and select the items your want to by.`
* **Corrected Copy:** `1. Browse our products and select the items you want to buy.`
* **Corrections Implemented:**
  * Removed incorrect apostrophe from **products** (changed from plural possessive to simple plural).
  * Changed the pronoun **your** to **you** to correct the grammar.
  * Corrected homophone spelling of **buy** (changed from *by*).

### Second Instruction Text
* **Original Copy:** `2. Add your chossen items to the cart and proceed to ceckout.`
* **Corrected Copy:** `2. Add your chosen items to the cart and proceed to checkout.`
* **Corrections Implemented:**
  * Corrected misspelling of **chosen** (changed from *chossen*).
  * Corrected misspelling of **checkout** (changed from *ceckout*).

### Third Instruction Text
* **Original Copy:** `3. Compleat the payment and recive your order cofirmation email.`
* **Corrected Copy:** `3. Complete the payment and receive your order confirmation email.`
* **Corrections Implemented:**
  * Corrected misspelling of **Complete** (changed from *Compleat*).
  * Corrected misspelling of **receive** (changed from *recive*).
  * Corrected misspelling of **confirmation** (changed from *cofirmation*).

---

## 2. Visual & Layout Specifications

### Layout Integrity
* **Status:** Verified (No Issues)
* **Specification:** 
  * The vertical alignment and spacing of the bulleted instruction list must remain perfectly centered within the white content container.
  * Padding around the list container must maintain a minimum of `24px` on the left and right borders to prevent text clipping across various screen sizes.
  * The header banner background color (`#2160C4` or equivalent brand blue) must remain visually consistent with the rest of the application's primary branding.

### Button & Navigation Controls
* **Primary Action (OK Button):** Centered horizontally at the bottom of the modal card with equal margin spacing above and below.
* **Dismiss Action (X Button):** Positioned in the top-right corner of the blue header bar, maintaining balanced padding from the top and right margins.

---

## 3. Visual Consistency Summary

| UI Element | Property | Verified / Approved State |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Header Text** | Font / Content | `"How to Use the Online Shop"` (Semibold, White, Centered) |
| **Instruction List** | Typography | Regular weight, dark slate body color, standard line height (`1.5`) for optimal readability. |
| **Footer Action** | Button Style | Rounded corners, medium gray fill with bold white `"OK"` text. |
| **Background Overlay** | Dimming | Standard `0.5` opacity dark overlay behind the modal to focus user attention. |

The system is functional with 0% error rate, but there is a major performance bottleneck: all calls are initiated over HTTP instead of HTTPS directly, triggering a mandatory 301 Redirect that accounts for ~47% of the total transaction response time. Fix the URL protocol in the test scripts before moving to production.","loadStatement":"Single-thread sequential test running for 125.8 seconds, executing 22 iterations of the 'Get verify successfull retrievel' transaction with an average pacing of 6 seconds.","executiveSummary":"The performance audit shows stable execution with zero errors. However, response times are artificially inflated by a redundant HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect (301) on every single transaction. Bypassing this redirect by configuring the JMeter script to target the HTTPS endpoints directly will reduce latency from an average of 1036 ms to approximately 533 ms, achieving a ~48% performance improvement. Additionally, the first request experienced high latency due to TCP and SSL handshake overheads.","technicalReport":{"errorRate":"0.00%","throughput":"0.17 TPS","metrics":[{"label":"Total Samples","value":"117"},{"label":"Average","value":"637.15"},{"label":"Min","value":"67"},{"label":"Max","value":"2623"},{"label":"Throughput","value":"0.51/sec"},{"label":"Total Transaction Iterations","value":"22"},{"label":"Avg Transaction Response Time","value":"1036 ms"},{"label":"Avg Redirect Overhead (301)","value":"484 ms"},{"label":"Avg Target response Time (200)","value":"533 ms"},{"label":"Warm-up Connection Overhead (Scenario 1-1)","value":"1154 ms"}],"latencyPercentiles":[{"label":"p50 (Median)","value":"971 ms"},{"label":"p90","value":"1150 ms"},{"label":"p95","value":"1336 ms"},{"label":"Max","value":"2623 ms"}],"bottlenecks":["HTTP-to-HTTPS Redirect loop: Every iteration of the transaction is calling 'http://fakestoreapi.com' instead of 'https://', adding an unnecessary network hop that averages 484 ms.","Initial connection overhead: The first thread iteration has a connect time of 1154 ms, representing SSL handshake and TCP connection setup overhead that is not reused initially."],"risks":["Unnecessary resource wastage: The server must handle double the request volume due to HTTP redirects.","Inaccurate baseline: Current baseline results are skewed by redirect overhead and do not represent actual target endpoint performance.","Undetected concurrency issues: Single-thread testing cannot validate system behavior, race conditions, or performance under multi-user production load."]}}

userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-1.1: When a multi-resource group is configured in PageCMS for specific appointment types, the system only applies consolidation logic to appointments of those types. Other same-day appointments for the same patient are processed independently. (Verify with practice having mixed grouped and non-grouped appointment types on same day)
• AC-1.2: The first consolidated reminder is not sent until the configured hold window has elapsed after the earliest appointment in the group is booked. (Test with 30-min, 1-hour, and 1-day window configurations)
• AC-1.3: When immediate send is configured on an appointment type and the patient self-schedules, the immediate confirmation fires. No second immediate reminder fires when the associated appointment is subsequently booked by staff. (Book both appointments within the hold window. Confirm single confirmation received)
• AC-1.4: When staff books an earlier same-day appointment after an immediate confirmation has already been sent, and an 'appointment updated' template is configured, the patient receives the update notification. (Test with and without update template configured. Confirm no notification sent when template absent)
• AC-1.5: All reminders after the initial confirmation (MSG-2, MSG-3) are sent only for the earliest appointment in the group. The later appointment does not receive any subsequent reminders. (Run full reminder sequence. Confirm emr_invite has exactly one active row per patient per appointment day within a group)
• AC-1.6: When the earliest appointment is cancelled, the next-earliest active appointment in the group is promoted and subsequent reminders continue for that appointment. (Cancel earliest. Confirm invite transfers. Confirm MSG-2 fires for promoted appointment)
• AC-1.7: When multi-resource grouping is not enabled for a practice or appointment type, existing reminder behavior is completely unchanged. (Regression test against practices without multi-resource configuration)
• Configurable Hold Window values must support: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, 2 calendar days. If all appointments in the group are booked before the window expires, the system sends the reminder immediately after the window closes.
userStories.summary: Smart Reminder Orchestration for Multi-Resource Same-Day Appointments
userStories.description: As a Practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences, so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders, and practices do not have to sacrifice their immediate confirmation workflow to enable multi-resource grouping.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-2.1: When a patient submits demographics on the consolidated landing page, the demographics API call is made against all appointment IDs in the group whose appointment types are configured to receive demographics in PageCMS. (Verify API call log shows correct appointment IDs. Confirm data appears in Athena against both appointments if both are configured for demographics)
• AC-2.2: When a patient submits HPI, ROS, or clinical screeners, the submission is stored in Yosi DB against the appointment ID whose appointment type is configured for those sections — not against the earliest appointment ID. (Ultrasound (9 AM) must NOT receive HPI/ROS/screener data. New Patient (10 AM) must receive it)
• AC-2.3: The appointment note 'patient has completed intake' is written to each appointment in the group separately via the correct appointment ID. (Confirm two separate appointment note API calls — one per appointment. Confirm notes visible in Athena for both)
• AC-2.4: When the New Patient encounter ID is generated at check-in, encounter-dependent sections stored against the New Patient appointment ID are pushed to Athena successfully. (Check in New Patient appointment. Confirm HPI, ROS, screeners appear in Athena encounter. Confirm Ultrasound encounter is unaffected)
• AC-2.5: In the case where an appointment outside the group will occur on the same day as a group, form sections for the outside-appointment will be updated to their respective appointment (existing behavior).
• AC-2.6: For practices not using multi-resource grouping, form submission routing is completely unchanged. (Full regression on single-appointment practices)
userStories.summary: Route Intake Paperwork Submissions to Correct Appointment Based on Appointment Type
userStories.description: As a Clinical provider and front desk staff at an OBGYN practice, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on which appointment type that form section belongs to, so that when a patient checks in for their New Patient appointment, the provider sees the completed HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners against that encounter — not against the earlier Ultrasound appointment — and front desk staff can confirm completion status per appointment accurately.

As a Patient with multiple same-day appointments at an OBGYN practice, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organised so I know what to complete for which visit, so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion about which forms belong to which appointment, and I understand the full picture of my visit day including the correct arrival time.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-3.1: When a patient with two same-day grouped appointments clicks the reminder link, the landing page displays both appointments in chronological order with their time, type, and provider. (Verify with Ultrasound 9 AM + New Patient 10 AM. Confirm 9 AM appears first with 'arrive here first' indicator)
• AC-3.2: Form sections displayed under each appointment match the PageCMS appointment type configuration for that appointment type. (Ultrasound must show demographics only. New Patient must show full intake. No cross-contamination)
• AC-3.3: Shared form sections (e.g. demographics) are displayed once and submitted to all appointments configured to receive them. The patient is not asked to enter the same information twice. (Submit demographics once. Confirm API posts against both appointment IDs)
• AC-3.4: If one appointment in the group is cancelled after the reminder is sent, the cancelled appointment does not appear on the landing page when the patient clicks the link. (Cancel Ultrasound after reminder sent. Confirm only New Patient appears on landing page)
• AC-3.5: If the sibling lookup API call fails or times out, the patient sees only the single appointment from the link token. No error message is displayed. (Simulate API timeout. Confirm graceful single-appointment fallback)
• AC-3.6: For patients with appointments on different days, the landing page shows only the appointment matching the token date. No other-day appointments appear. (Verify with patient having appointments on two different dates)
• AC-3.7: For single-appointment patients or appointment types not in a multi-resource group, the landing page renders identically to today's experience. (Full regression on non-grouped appointment types)
• The backend API endpoint GET /patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token} must fetch all active same-day appointments in the same multi-resource group on the same calendar date, excluding cancelled/rescheduled appointments.
userStories.summary: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page

userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-4.1: When a patient has two same-day appointments in a multi-resource group, the dashboard shows them as a grouped unit with the earliest appointment as the primary row and the later appointment visually associated beneath it. (Verify on both today view and a future date view. Confirm grouping does not appear for appointments on different days)
• AC-4.2: The combined paperwork status shows 'All Complete' only when all form sections across all appointments in the group have been submitted. (Submit only Ultrasound paperwork. Confirm status shows 'Partially Complete'. Submit New Patient paperwork. Confirm status updates to 'All Complete')
• AC-4.3: The combined paperwork status shows 'Partially Complete' when at least one section is complete and at least one is incomplete across the group. (Submit demographics only. Confirm status shows 'Partially Complete')

• AC-4.6: Patients with a single appointment or with appointment types not in a multi-resource group appear on the dashboard exactly as today — no grouping applied. (Full regression on non-grouped appointment types and single-appointment patients)
• AC-4.7: The paperwork completion status on the dashboard accurately reflects the corrected per-appointment routing from Story 2. Ultrasound shows its own completion, New Patient shows its own completion. (Complete only Ultrasound paperwork. Confirm dashboard shows Ultrasound complete, New Patient incomplete. Complete New Patient paperwork. Confirm both show complete)

userStories.summary: Input Requirements Doc (Epic_ Multi-Resource Appointment Enhancement.pdf)

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • PageCMS must allow practice administrators to define multi-resource groups at the appointment type level (e.g., 'Ultrasound ID 3 + New Patient ID 1 = Group A'). • A single appointment type can belong to only one multi-resource group per practice. • Appointment types not in any group must continue to behave as standalone appointments with no change to existing logic. • The system must support configuring a consolidation hold window per practice (supported values: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, 2 calendar days), defaulting to 1 calendar day. • If all appointments in the group are booked before the hold window expires, the system must send the consolidated reminder immediately after the window closes. • When a patient self-schedules via Yosi Scheduler, an immediate confirmation message must fire for that appointment regardless of the multi-resource configuration. Subsequent reminders (MSG-2, MSG-3, etc.) must be sent only to the earliest appointment in the group and follow the consolidated cadence. • If staff books an earlier same-day appointment after the immediate send has fired, and an 'appointment updated' template is configured in PageCMS, an update notification must be sent to the patient. • If the earliest appointment in a group is cancelled, the system must promote the next-earliest active appointment, continue subsequent reminders for it, and send a promotion notification if configured. If no other active appointments remain, the invite must be closed and reminders stopped.
userStories.summary: MRA-001: Smart Reminder Orchestration for Multi-Resource Same-Day Appointments
userStories.description: As a Practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences, so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders, and practices do not have to sacrifice their immediate confirmation workflow to enable multi-resource grouping.

As a Clinical provider and front desk staff at an OBGYN practice, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on which appointment type that form section belongs to, so that when a patient checks in for their New Patient appointment, the provider sees the completed HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners against that encounter (not against the earlier Ultrasound appointment) and front desk staff can confirm completion status per appointment accurately.
userStories.summary: MRA-002: Route Intake Paperwork Submissions to the Correct Appointment Based on Appointment Type
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • PageCMS must support associating each form section (page) with one or more appointment type IDs. • When a patient submits a form section, the system must route the submission to the appointment ID whose appointment type matches the form section's PageCMS mapping. • The appointment note update ('patient has completed intake') must be written separately per appointment in the group. • Demographics and other sections shared across multiple appointment types in the group must be written to all relevant appointment IDs. • If an appointment outside the group occurs on the same day as a group, form sections for that outside appointment must be updated to their respective appointment. • Encounter-dependent sections (HPI, ROS, screeners) must be stored in the database with patient_id, practice_id, appointment_id, and encounter_id = null. • When the EMR check-in trigger fires and an encounter ID is received, the system must match it against the stored appointment_id and push the clinical data to the correct Athena encounter.

• Introduce a GET endpoint `/patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token}` to return all active appointments for the patient on the same calendar date that belong to the same multi-resource group. • Cancelled or rescheduled appointments must be excluded from the sibling lookup. • If only one appointment is returned, the landing page must render in its standard single-appointment view. • If multiple appointments are returned, render a consolidated view in chronological order (earliest first). • Each appointment must be clearly labeled with its time, and the earliest appointment must be visually distinguished as the primary arrival appointment (e.g., 'Please arrive for this appointment first'). • Form sections must be grouped under their respective appointment, allowing the patient to complete paperwork sequentially in one session. • Shared sections (e.g., demographics) must display only once and submit to all configured appointments in the group. • The page must use the PageCMS configuration of the earliest appointment as the base styling and branding. • If the sibling lookup API fails or times out, the page must fall back to rendering the single appointment from the token without showing an error to the patient.
userStories.summary: MRA-003: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
userStories.description: As a Patient with multiple same-day appointments at an OBGYN practice, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organised so I know what to complete for which visit, so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion about which forms belong to which appointment, and I understand the full picture of my visit day including the correct arrival time.

As a Front desk staff member at an OBGYN practice using the Yosi dashboard, I want to see all same-day appointments associated to a patient in a single grouped view, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, and the ability to click through to each appointment's detail, so that I can confirm at a glance that a patient has completed all required paperwork before check-in, understand the full schedule for that patient's visit day, and take action on any individual appointment without switching views.
userStories.summary: MRA-004: Show Associated Same-Day Appointments and Consolidated Paperwork Status on Practice Dashboard
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • On both today's and future dashboard views, same-day appointments belonging to the same multi-resource group must be displayed as a grouped unit anchored to the earliest appointment as the primary row, with associated appointments visually nested beneath it. • Each associated appointment must display: appointment time, appointment type, provider name, and individual paperwork completion status. • Display a combined paperwork status indicator for the group: 'All Complete' (all form sections across all appointments in the group submitted), 'Partially Complete' (at least one form section submitted, but at least one required section remains incomplete), or 'Not Started' (no forms submitted). • Status logic must reflect the separate per-appointment routing from Story 2. • Clicking any appointment in the group must open the existing appointment detail view for that specific appointment, maintaining all existing actions. • Grouping must only apply to appointments occurring on the same viewed day. • Cancelled appointments within a group must remain visible with a cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed. • Patients with single appointments or non-grouped appointment types must appear exactly as they do today with no grouping applied.

userStories.description: As a practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences, so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders.
userStories.summary: MRA-001: Smart Reminder Orchestration and Configuration
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. PageCMS Configuration: PageCMS must allow practice administrators to define multi-resource groups at the appointment type level (e.g., 'Ultrasound ID 3 + New Patient ID 1 = Group A').
2. Group Constraints: A single appointment type can belong to only one multi-resource group per practice. Appointment types not configured in any group must continue to behave as standalone appointments with no changes to existing logic.
3. Configurable Hold Window: PageCMS must allow the hold window to be configured in minutes, hours, or days per practice, supporting values of: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, and 2 calendar days. The default value must remain 1 calendar day for backward compatibility.
4. Consolidation Timing: The first consolidated reminder must not be sent until the configured hold window has elapsed after the earliest appointment in the group is booked. If all appointments in the group are booked before the hold window expires, the system must send the consolidated reminder immediately after the window closes.
5. Immediate Send Handling: If a patient self-schedules via the Yosi Scheduler and an immediate message is configured, an immediate confirmation must fire for that appointment. No second immediate reminder should fire when the associated appointment is subsequently booked by staff within the hold window.
6. Promotion Logic: When the earliest appointment in a multi-resource group is cancelled, the system must identify the next-earliest active appointment in the group and promote it. Subsequent reminders (such as MSG-2 and MSG-3) must continue for the promoted appointment. If a promotion notification template is configured, a notification must be sent to the patient.
7. Closing Invites: If no other active appointments remain in the group after a cancellation, the invite must be closed and no further reminders sent.

userStories.description: As a clinical provider and front desk staff, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on the PageCMS mapping, so that completed clinical screeners are visible against the correct encounter in Athena and front desk staff can confirm completion status accurately.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Appointment-to-Form Mapping: PageCMS must support associating each form section (page) to one or more appointment type IDs.
2. Submission Routing: When a patient submits a form section on the consolidated landing page, the system must route the submission to the appointment ID whose appointment type matches the form section's PageCMS mapping.
3. Shared Sections: Demographics and other sections configured as shared across multiple appointment types in the group must be written to all relevant appointment IDs.
4. Appointment Notes: The appointment note update indicating 'patient has completed intake' must be written separately per appointment (one note per appointment in the group).
5. Encounter-Dependent Storage: Encounter-dependent sections (such as HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners) must be stored in Yosi DB with patient_id, practice_id, appointment_id, and encounter_id set to null until check-in.
6. Check-In Integration: When the Athena check-in trigger fires and an encounter ID is received, the system must match it against the stored appointment ID and push the encounter-dependent data to the correct Athena encounter. If an encounter ID arrives for an appointment that has no encounter-dependent data stored, the system must take no action.
userStories.summary: MRA-002: Paperwork Association and Submission Routing
MRA-003: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Sibling Lookup API: The landing page must call the backend API endpoint `GET /patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token}` to fetch all active same-day appointments for the patient in the same multi-resource group.
2. Lookup Exclusions: Cancelled or rescheduled appointments, and appointments scheduled on different calendar dates, must be excluded from the response.
3. Consolidated UI Rendering: If the sibling lookup returns multiple appointments, the landing page must render a consolidated view showing all same-day appointments in chronological order (earliest first).
4. Primary Arrival Distinction: The earliest appointment must be visually distinguished on the page as the primary arrival appointment (e.g., displaying an instruction like 'Please arrive for this appointment first').
5. Section Grouping and Sequencing: Form sections must be grouped under their respective appointments and completed sequentially. Shared sections must be shown only once and submitted to all relevant appointment IDs behind the scenes.
6. Styling & Branding: The page must utilize the PageCMS configuration of the earliest appointment as the base styling and branding, while rendering appointment-type-specific content per section.
7. Fallback Behavior: If the sibling lookup API call fails or times out, the page must gracefully fall back to rendering the single appointment from the token without showing errors to the patient. If all appointments in the group are cancelled, the page must display a message directing the patient to contact the practice.
userStories.description: As a patient with multiple same-day appointments, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organized, so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion.

userStories.summary: MRA-004: Practice Dashboard Associated Same-Day Appointment Grouping
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Grouped Display: On both today's and future date dashboard views, appointments belonging to the same multi-resource group must be displayed as a grouped unit anchored to the earliest appointment as the primary row, with associated appointments nested beneath.
2. Display Fields: Each associated appointment card/row in the group must display the appointment time, appointment type, provider name, and individual paperwork completion status.
3. Combined Paperwork Status Logic: The group as a whole must show a combined paperwork status indicator: 'All Complete' (all form sections across all appointments in the group are submitted), 'Partially Complete' (at least one form section has been submitted, but at least one required section remains incomplete), or 'Not Started' (no form sections submitted for any appointment in the group).
4. Detail View Navigation: Clicking any appointment in the group must open the existing appointment detail view for that specific appointment, preserving all actions (view paperwork, send manual reminder, view patient profile).
5. Grouping Date Boundaries: Grouping must be strictly based on the appointment date being viewed. Appointments on different days for the same patient must not be grouped together.
6. Cancelled Appointments: Cancelled appointments within a group must remain visible with a visual cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed to provide staff with operational context.
7. Standalone & Non-Grouped Behavior: Patients with single appointments or appointment types not associated with a multi-resource group must appear on the dashboard exactly as they do today with no grouping applied.
userStories.description: As a front desk staff member, I want to see all same-day appointments associated with a patient in a single grouped view on the practice dashboard, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, so that I can confirm paperwork completion and understand the full schedule at a glance before check-in.

userStories.summary: Smart Reminder Orchestration for Multi-Resource Same-Day Appointments
userStories.description: As a practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders, and practices do not have to sacrifice their immediate confirmation workflow to enable multi-resource grouping.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • When a multi-resource group is configured in PageCMS for specific appointment types, the system only applies consolidation logic to appointments of those types. Other same-day appointments for the same patient are processed independently. • PageCMS must allow practice administrators to define multi-resource groups at the appointment type level (e.g., 'Ultrasound ID 3 + New Patient ID 1 = Group A'). • A single appointment type can belong to only one multi-resource group per practice. • Appointment types not in any group continue to behave as standalone appointments with no change to existing logic. • The existing practice-wide multi-resource flag is deprecated once all practices are migrated to appointment-type-level configuration. • The first consolidated reminder is not sent until the configured hold window has elapsed after the earliest appointment in the group is booked. • PageCMS must allow the hold window to be configured in minutes, hours, or days per practice, with supported values including 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, and 2 calendar days. • The default value for the hold window remains 1 calendar day for backward compatibility. • The hold window defines how long the system waits after the first appointment in a group is booked before sending the first reminder, to allow time for all associated appointments to be scheduled. • If all appointments in the group are booked before the hold window expires, the system will send the consolidated reminder immediately after the window closes without waiting for the full configured duration. • When immediate send is configured on an appointment type and the patient self-schedules via Yosi Scheduler, the immediate confirmation fires. No second immediate reminder fires when the associated appointment is subsequently booked by staff. • All subsequent reminders (MSG-2, MSG-3, and beyond) are sent only to the earliest appointment in the group and follow the consolidated cadence. • If staff books an earlier same-day appointment after the immediate send has already fired, and an 'appointment updated' template is configured for the practice in PageCMS, a notification is sent to the patient informing them of the earlier arrival time. This 'appointment updated' notification is a new configurable message type and is optional. • When the earliest appointment in a multi-resource group is cancelled, the system identifies the next-earliest active appointment in the group. • Subsequent reminders continue for the promoted appointment. • If a promotion notification template is configured, the patient is notified. • If no other active appointments remain in the group, the invite is closed and no further reminders are sent. • When multi-resource grouping is not enabled for a practice or appointment type, existing reminder behavior is completely unchanged.

userStories.summary: Route Intake Paperwork Submissions to the Correct Appointment Based on Appointment Type
userStories.description: As a clinical provider and front desk staff at an OBGYN practice, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on which appointment type that form section belongs to so that when a patient checks in for their New Patient appointment, the provider sees the completed HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners against that encounter — not against the earlier Ultrasound appointment — and front desk staff can confirm completion status per appointment accurately.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • Each form section (page) in PageCMS must be associated with one or more appointment type IDs. • When a patient lands on the consolidated paperwork page, the system determines which form sections to display for each appointment based on this mapping. • When a patient submits a form section, the system routes the submission to the appointment ID whose appointment type matches the form section's PageCMS mapping. • When a patient submits demographics on the consolidated landing page, the demographics API call is made against all appointment IDs in the group whose appointment types are configured to receive demographics in PageCMS. • Demographics and other sections shared across multiple appointment types in the group are written to all relevant appointment IDs. • When a patient submits HPI, ROS, or clinical screeners, the submission is stored in Yosi DB against the appointment ID whose appointment type is configured for those sections — not against the earliest appointment ID. • Encounter-dependent sections are stored in Yosi DB with patient_id, practice_id, appointment_id (from appointment type mapping), and encounter_id = null until check-in. • The appointment note 'patient has completed intake' is written to each appointment in the group separately via the correct appointment ID. • When the Athena check-in trigger fires and an encounter ID is received, the system matches it against the stored appointment_id and pushes the data. • If the encounter ID arrives for the New Patient appointment (10 AM), encounter-dependent data stored against the New Patient appointment_id is pushed, while data stored against the Ultrasound appointment_id (e.g., demographics) is unaffected. • If an encounter ID arrives for an appointment that has no encounter-dependent data stored (e.g., Ultrasound), the system takes no action for those sections. • In the case where an appointment outside the group will occur on the same day as a group, form sections for the outside-appointment will be updated to their respective appointment (existing behavior). • For practices not using multi-resource grouping, form submission routing is userStories.summary: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
userStories.description: As a patient with multiple same-day appointments at an OBGYN practice, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organised so I know what to complete for which visit so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion about which forms belong to which appointment, and I understand the full picture of my visit day including the correct arrival time.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • A new endpoint GET /patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token} must return all active appointments for the patient on the same calendar date that belong to the same multi-resource group. • Cancelled or rescheduled appointments are excluded from the response of the API call. • Appointments on different days are never included regardless of patient or practice. • If the sibling lookup returns only one appointment (single-appointment patient or non-grouped type), the landing page renders as today with no change to the existing experience. • When a patient with two same-day grouped appointments clicks the reminder link, the landing page displays both appointments in chronological order with their time, type, and provider. • When the sibling lookup returns multiple appointments, the landing page renders a consolidated view showing all same-day appointments in chronological order, earliest first. • Each appointment is clearly labelled with its time and action button. • The earliest appointment is visually distinguished as the primary arrival appointment (e.g., 'Please arrive for this appointment first'). • Form sections are grouped under their respective appointment. The patient completes paperwork for each appointment in sequence within one session. • Form sections displayed under each appointment match the PageCMS appointment type configuration for that appointment type. • Shared sections (e.g., demographics) that apply to multiple appointments are shown once and submitted to all relevant appointments — the patient is not asked to re-enter the same information twice. • The page uses the PageCMS configuration of the earliest appointment as the base styling and branding, with appointment-type-specific content (instructions, provider notes) rendered per section. • If one appointment in the group is cancelled after the reminder is sent, the cancelled appointment does not appear on the landing page when the patient clicks the link. • If the sibling lookup API call fails or times out, the patient sees only the single appointment from the link token, with no error message displayed. • If all appointments in the group are cancelled by the time the patient clicks the link, the page displays an appropriate message directing the patient to contact the practice. • The link remains valid and shows the current state of appointments at the time of access — it is not a static snapshot. • For patients with appointments on different days, the landing page shows only the appointment matching the token date, with no other-day appointments appearing. • For single-appointment patients or appointment types not in a multi-resource group, the landing page renders identically to today's experience.

userStories.summary: Show Associated Same-Day Appointments and Consolidated Paperwork Status on Practice Dashboard
userStories.description: As a front desk staff member at an OBGYN practice using the Yosi dashboard, I want to see all same-day appointments associated to a patient in a single grouped view, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, and the ability to click through to each appointment's detail so that I can confirm at a glance that a patient has completed all required paperwork before check-in, understand the full schedule for that patient's visit day, and take action on any individual appointment without switching views.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • On both today's dashboard view and future date views, appointments belonging to the same multi-resource group are displayed as a grouped unit anchored to the earliest appointment. • When a patient has two same-day appointments in a multi-resource group, the dashboard shows them as a grouped unit with the earliest appointment as the primary row and the later appointment visually associated beneath it. • The earliest appointment is the primary row, and associated appointments are visually nested beneath it. • Each associated appointment shows: appointment time, appointment type, provider name, and individual paperwork completion status. • The group as a whole shows a combined paperwork status indicator: All Complete, Partially Complete, or Not Started. • The combined paperwork status shows 'All Complete' only when all form sections across all appointments in the group have been submitted. • The combined paperwork status shows 'Partially Complete' when at least one form section has been submitted but at least one required section remains incomplete across any appointment in the group. • The combined paperwork status shows 'Not Started' when no form sections have been submitted for any appointment in the group. • The paperwork completion status on the dashboard accurately reflects the corrected per-appointment routing from Story 2 (e.g., Ultrasound shows its own completion, New Patient shows its own completion). • Clicking any appointment in the group (earliest or associated) opens the existing appointment detail view for that specific appointment. • All existing actions available in the appointment detail view (e.g., view paperwork, send manual reminder, view patient profile) are available for associated appointments. • There is no change to the appointment detail view itself in this story. • The grouping is based on the appointment date being viewed; a patient with appointments on different days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday) does not have those grouped together. • A cancelled appointment within a group remains visible on the dashboard with a cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed, to give staff context. • Patients with a single appointment or with appointment types not in a multi-resource group appear on the dashboard exactly as today, with no grouping applied.

Additional Context / Guidelines:

userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-1.1: When a multi-resource group is configured in PageCMS for specific appointment types, the system only applies consolidation logic to appointments of those types. Other same-day appointments for the same patient are processed independently. (Verify with practice having mixed grouped and non-grouped appointment types on same day)
• AC-1.2: The first consolidated reminder is not sent until the configured hold window has elapsed after the earliest appointment in the group is booked. (Test with 30-min, 1-hour, and 1-day window configurations)
• AC-1.3: When immediate send is configured on an appointment type and the patient self-schedules, the immediate confirmation fires. No second immediate reminder fires when the associated appointment is subsequently booked by staff. (Book both appointments within the hold window. Confirm single confirmation received)
• AC-1.4: When staff books an earlier same-day appointment after an immediate confirmation has already been sent, and an 'appointment updated' template is configured, the patient receives the update notification. (Test with and without update template configured. Confirm no notification sent when template absent)
• AC-1.5: All reminders after the initial confirmation (MSG-2, MSG-3) are sent only for the earliest appointment in the group. The later appointment does not receive any subsequent reminders. (Run full reminder sequence. Confirm emr_invite has exactly one active row per patient per appointment day within a group)
• AC-1.6: When the earliest appointment is cancelled, the next-earliest active appointment in the group is promoted and subsequent reminders continue for that appointment. (Cancel earliest. Confirm invite transfers. Confirm MSG-2 fires for promoted appointment)
• AC-1.7: When multi-resource grouping is not enabled for a practice or appointment type, existing reminder behavior is completely unchanged. (Regression test against practices without multi-resource configuration)
• Configurable Hold Window values must support: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, 2 calendar days. If all appointments in the group are booked before the window expires, the system sends the reminder immediately after the window closes.
userStories.summary: Smart Reminder Orchestration for Multi-Resource Same-Day Appointments
userStories.description: As a Practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences, so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders, and practices do not have to sacrifice their immediate confirmation workflow to enable multi-resource grouping.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-2.1: When a patient submits demographics on the consolidated landing page, the demographics API call is made against all appointment IDs in the group whose appointment types are configured to receive demographics in PageCMS. (Verify API call log shows correct appointment IDs. Confirm data appears in Athena against both appointments if both are configured for demographics)
• AC-2.2: When a patient submits HPI, ROS, or clinical screeners, the submission is stored in Yosi DB against the appointment ID whose appointment type is configured for those sections — not against the earliest appointment ID. (Ultrasound (9 AM) must NOT receive HPI/ROS/screener data. New Patient (10 AM) must receive it)
• AC-2.3: The appointment note 'patient has completed intake' is written to each appointment in the group separately via the correct appointment ID. (Confirm two separate appointment note API calls — one per appointment. Confirm notes visible in Athena for both)
• AC-2.4: When the New Patient encounter ID is generated at check-in, encounter-dependent sections stored against the New Patient appointment ID are pushed to Athena successfully. (Check in New Patient appointment. Confirm HPI, ROS, screeners appear in Athena encounter. Confirm Ultrasound encounter is unaffected)
• AC-2.5: In the case where an appointment outside the group will occur on the same day as a group, form sections for the outside-appointment will be updated to their respective appointment (existing behavior).
• AC-2.6: For practices not using multi-resource grouping, form submission routing is completely unchanged. (Full regression on single-appointment practices)
userStories.summary: Route Intake Paperwork Submissions to Correct Appointment Based on Appointment Type
userStories.description: As a Clinical provider and front desk staff at an OBGYN practice, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on which appointment type that form section belongs to, so that when a patient checks in for their New Patient appointment, the provider sees the completed HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners against that encounter — not against the earlier Ultrasound appointment — and front desk staff can confirm completion status per appointment accurately.

As a Patient with multiple same-day appointments at an OBGYN practice, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organised so I know what to complete for which visit, so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion about which forms belong to which appointment, and I understand the full picture of my visit day including the correct arrival time.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-3.1: When a patient with two same-day grouped appointments clicks the reminder link, the landing page displays both appointments in chronological order with their time, type, and provider. (Verify with Ultrasound 9 AM + New Patient 10 AM. Confirm 9 AM appears first with 'arrive here first' indicator)
• AC-3.2: Form sections displayed under each appointment match the PageCMS appointment type configuration for that appointment type. (Ultrasound must show demographics only. New Patient must show full intake. No cross-contamination)
• AC-3.3: Shared form sections (e.g. demographics) are displayed once and submitted to all appointments configured to receive them. The patient is not asked to enter the same information twice. (Submit demographics once. Confirm API posts against both appointment IDs)
• AC-3.4: If one appointment in the group is cancelled after the reminder is sent, the cancelled appointment does not appear on the landing page when the patient clicks the link. (Cancel Ultrasound after reminder sent. Confirm only New Patient appears on landing page)
• AC-3.5: If the sibling lookup API call fails or times out, the patient sees only the single appointment from the link token. No error message is displayed. (Simulate API timeout. Confirm graceful single-appointment fallback)
• AC-3.6: For patients with appointments on different days, the landing page shows only the appointment matching the token date. No other-day appointments appear. (Verify with patient having appointments on two different dates)
• AC-3.7: For single-appointment patients or appointment types not in a multi-resource group, the landing page renders identically to today's experience. (Full regression on non-grouped appointment types)
• The backend API endpoint GET /patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token} must fetch all active same-day appointments in the same multi-resource group on the same calendar date, excluding cancelled/rescheduled appointments.
userStories.summary: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
Show Associated Same-Day Appointments and Consolidated Paperwork Status on Practice Dashboard
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
• AC-4.1: When a patient has two same-day appointments in a multi-resource group, the dashboard shows them as a grouped unit with the earliest appointment as the primary row and the later appointment visually associated beneath it. (Verify on both today view and a future date view. Confirm grouping does not appear for appointments on different days)
• AC-4.2: The combined paperwork status shows 'All Complete' only when all form sections across all appointments in the group have been submitted. (Submit only Ultrasound paperwork. Confirm status shows 'Partially Complete'. Submit New Patient paperwork. Confirm status updates to 'All Complete')
• AC-4.3: The combined paperwork status shows 'Partially Complete' when at least one section is complete and at least one is incomplete across the group. (Submit demographics only. Confirm status shows 'Partially Complete')
• AC-4.4: Clicking an associated appointment in the group opens the appointment detail view for that specific appointment with all existing actions available. (Click Ultrasound row. Confirm Ultrasound detail opens. Click New Patient row. Confirm New Patient detail opens)
• AC-4.5: A cancelled appointment within a group remains visible on the dashboard with a cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed. (Cancel one appointment in a group. Confirm it shows as cancelled in the group view, not removed)
• AC-4.6: Patients with a single appointment or with appointment types not in a multi-resource group appear on the dashboard exactly as today — no grouping applied. (Full regression on non-grouped appointment types and single-appointment patients)
• AC-4.7: The paperwork completion status on the dashboard accurately reflects the corrected per-appointment routing from Story 2. Ultrasound shows its own completion, New Patient shows its own completion. (Complete only Ultrasound paperwork. Confirm dashboard shows Ultrasound complete, New Patient incomplete. Complete New Patient paperwork. Confirm both show complete)
userStories.description: As a Front desk staff member at an OBGYN practice using the Yosi dashboard, I want to see all same-day appointments associated to a patient in a single grouped view, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, and the ability to click through to each appointment's detail, so that I can confirm at a glance that a patient has completed all required paperwork before check-in, understand the full schedule for that patient's visit day, and take action on any individual appointment without switching views.

userStories.summary: Input Requirements Doc (Epic_ Multi-Resource Appointment Enhancement.pdf)

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • PageCMS must allow practice administrators to define multi-resource groups at the appointment type level (e.g., 'Ultrasound ID 3 + New Patient ID 1 = Group A'). • A single appointment type can belong to only one multi-resource group per practice. • Appointment types not in any group must continue to behave as standalone appointments with no change to existing logic. • The system must support configuring a consolidation hold window per practice (supported values: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, 2 calendar days), defaulting to 1 calendar day. • If all appointments in the group are booked before the hold window expires, the system must send the consolidated reminder immediately after the window closes. • When a patient self-schedules via Yosi Scheduler, an immediate confirmation message must fire for that appointment regardless of the multi-resource configuration. Subsequent reminders (MSG-2, MSG-3, etc.) must be sent only to the earliest appointment in the group and follow the consolidated cadence. • If staff books an earlier same-day appointment after the immediate send has fired, and an 'appointment updated' template is configured in PageCMS, an update notification must be sent to the patient. • If the earliest appointment in a group is cancelled, the system must promote the next-earliest active appointment, continue subsequent reminders for it, and send a promotion notification if configured. If no other active appointments remain, the invite must be closed and reminders stopped.
userStories.summary: MRA-001: Smart Reminder Orchestration for Multi-Resource Same-Day Appointments
userStories.description: As a Practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences, so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders, and practices do not have to sacrifice their immediate confirmation workflow to enable multi-resource grouping.

As a Clinical provider and front desk staff at an OBGYN practice, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on which appointment type that form section belongs to, so that when a patient checks in for their New Patient appointment, the provider sees the completed HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners against that encounter (not against the earlier Ultrasound appointment) and front desk staff can confirm completion status per appointment accurately.
userStories.summary: MRA-002: Route Intake Paperwork Submissions to the Correct Appointment Based on Appointment Type
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • PageCMS must support associating each form section (page) with one or more appointment type IDs. • When a patient submits a form section, the system must route the submission to the appointment ID whose appointment type matches the form section's PageCMS mapping. • The appointment note update ('patient has completed intake') must be written separately per appointment in the group. • Demographics and other sections shared across multiple appointment types in the group must be written to all relevant appointment IDs. • If an appointment outside the group occurs on the same day as a group, form sections for that outside appointment must be updated to their respective appointment. • Encounter-dependent sections (HPI, ROS, screeners) must be stored in the database with patient_id, practice_id, appointment_id, and encounter_id = null. • When the EMR check-in trigger fires and an encounter ID is received, the system must match it against the stored appointment_id and push the clinical data to the correct Athena encounter.

• Introduce a GET endpoint `/patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token}` to return all active appointments for the patient on the same calendar date that belong to the same multi-resource group. • Cancelled or rescheduled appointments must be excluded from the sibling lookup. • If only one appointment is returned, the landing page must render in its standard single-appointment view. • If multiple appointments are returned, render a consolidated view in chronological order (earliest first). • Each appointment must be clearly labeled with its time, and the earliest appointment must be visually distinguished as the primary arrival appointment (e.g., 'Please arrive for this appointment first'). • Form sections must be grouped under their respective appointment, allowing the patient to complete paperwork sequentially in one session. • Shared sections (e.g., demographics) must display only once and submit to all configured appointments in the group. • The page must use the PageCMS configuration of the earliest appointment as the base styling and branding. • If the sibling lookup API fails or times out, the page must fall back to rendering the single appointment from the token without showing an error to the patient.
userStories.summary: MRA-003: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
userStories.description: As a Patient with multiple same-day appointments at an OBGYN practice, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organised so I know what to complete for which visit, so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion about which forms belong to which appointment, and I understand the full picture of my visit day including the correct arrival time.

As a Front desk staff member at an OBGYN practice using the Yosi dashboard, I want to see all same-day appointments associated to a patient in a single grouped view, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, and the ability to click through to each appointment's detail, so that I can confirm at a glance that a patient has completed all required paperwork before check-in, understand the full schedule for that patient's visit day, and take action on any individual appointment without switching views.
userStories.summary: MRA-004: Show Associated Same-Day Appointments and Consolidated Paperwork Status on Practice Dashboard
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • On both today's and future dashboard views, same-day appointments belonging to the same multi-resource group must be displayed as a grouped unit anchored to the earliest appointment as the primary row, with associated appointments visually nested beneath it. • Each associated appointment must display: appointment time, appointment type, provider name, and individual paperwork completion status. • Display a combined paperwork status indicator for the group: 'All Complete' (all form sections across all appointments in the group submitted), 'Partially Complete' (at least one form section submitted, but at least one required section remains incomplete), or 'Not Started' (no forms submitted). • Status logic must reflect the separate per-appointment routing from Story 2. • Clicking any appointment in the group must open the existing appointment detail view for that specific appointment, maintaining all existing actions. • Grouping must only apply to appointments occurring on the same viewed day. • Cancelled appointments within a group must remain visible with a cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed. • Patients with single appointments or non-grouped appointment types must appear exactly as they do today with no grouping applied.
