userStories.description: As a practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences, so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders.
userStories.summary: MRA-001: Smart Reminder Orchestration and Configuration
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. PageCMS Configuration: PageCMS must allow practice administrators to define multi-resource groups at the appointment type level (e.g., 'Ultrasound ID 3 + New Patient ID 1 = Group A').
2. Group Constraints: A single appointment type can belong to only one multi-resource group per practice. Appointment types not configured in any group must continue to behave as standalone appointments with no changes to existing logic.
3. Configurable Hold Window: PageCMS must allow the hold window to be configured in minutes, hours, or days per practice, supporting values of: 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, and 2 calendar days. The default value must remain 1 calendar day for backward compatibility.
4. Consolidation Timing: The first consolidated reminder must not be sent until the configured hold window has elapsed after the earliest appointment in the group is booked. If all appointments in the group are booked before the hold window expires, the system must send the consolidated reminder immediately after the window closes.
5. Immediate Send Handling: If a patient self-schedules via the Yosi Scheduler and an immediate message is configured, an immediate confirmation must fire for that appointment. No second immediate reminder should fire when the associated appointment is subsequently booked by staff within the hold window.
6. Promotion Logic: When the earliest appointment in a multi-resource group is cancelled, the system must identify the next-earliest active appointment in the group and promote it. Subsequent reminders (such as MSG-2 and MSG-3) must continue for the promoted appointment. If a promotion notification template is configured, a notification must be sent to the patient.
7. Closing Invites: If no other active appointments remain in the group after a cancellation, the invite must be closed and no further reminders sent.

userStories.description: As a clinical provider and front desk staff, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on the PageCMS mapping, so that completed clinical screeners are visible against the correct encounter in Athena and front desk staff can confirm completion status accurately.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Appointment-to-Form Mapping: PageCMS must support associating each form section (page) to one or more appointment type IDs.
2. Submission Routing: When a patient submits a form section on the consolidated landing page, the system must route the submission to the appointment ID whose appointment type matches the form section's PageCMS mapping.
3. Shared Sections: Demographics and other sections configured as shared across multiple appointment types in the group must be written to all relevant appointment IDs.
4. Appointment Notes: The appointment note update indicating 'patient has completed intake' must be written separately per appointment (one note per appointment in the group).
5. Encounter-Dependent Storage: Encounter-dependent sections (such as HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners) must be stored in Yosi DB with patient_id, practice_id, appointment_id, and encounter_id set to null until check-in.
6. Check-In Integration: When the Athena check-in trigger fires and an encounter ID is received, the system must match it against the stored appointment ID and push the encounter-dependent data to the correct Athena encounter. If an encounter ID arrives for an appointment that has no encounter-dependent data stored, the system must take no action.
userStories.summary: MRA-002: Paperwork Association and Submission Routing
MRA-003: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Sibling Lookup API: The landing page must call the backend API endpoint `GET /patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token}` to fetch all active same-day appointments for the patient in the same multi-resource group.
2. Lookup Exclusions: Cancelled or rescheduled appointments, and appointments scheduled on different calendar dates, must be excluded from the response.
3. Consolidated UI Rendering: If the sibling lookup returns multiple appointments, the landing page must render a consolidated view showing all same-day appointments in chronological order (earliest first).
4. Primary Arrival Distinction: The earliest appointment must be visually distinguished on the page as the primary arrival appointment (e.g., displaying an instruction like 'Please arrive for this appointment first').
5. Section Grouping and Sequencing: Form sections must be grouped under their respective appointments and completed sequentially. Shared sections must be shown only once and submitted to all relevant appointment IDs behind the scenes.
6. Styling & Branding: The page must utilize the PageCMS configuration of the earliest appointment as the base styling and branding, while rendering appointment-type-specific content per section.
7. Fallback Behavior: If the sibling lookup API call fails or times out, the page must gracefully fall back to rendering the single appointment from the token without showing errors to the patient. If all appointments in the group are cancelled, the page must display a message directing the patient to contact the practice.
userStories.description: As a patient with multiple same-day appointments, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organized, so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion.

userStories.summary: MRA-004: Practice Dashboard Associated Same-Day Appointment Grouping
userStories.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Grouped Display: On both today's and future date dashboard views, appointments belonging to the same multi-resource group must be displayed as a grouped unit anchored to the earliest appointment as the primary row, with associated appointments nested beneath.
2. Display Fields: Each associated appointment card/row in the group must display the appointment time, appointment type, provider name, and individual paperwork completion status.
3. Combined Paperwork Status Logic: The group as a whole must show a combined paperwork status indicator: 'All Complete' (all form sections across all appointments in the group are submitted), 'Partially Complete' (at least one form section has been submitted, but at least one required section remains incomplete), or 'Not Started' (no form sections submitted for any appointment in the group).
4. Detail View Navigation: Clicking any appointment in the group must open the existing appointment detail view for that specific appointment, preserving all actions (view paperwork, send manual reminder, view patient profile).
5. Grouping Date Boundaries: Grouping must be strictly based on the appointment date being viewed. Appointments on different days for the same patient must not be grouped together.
6. Cancelled Appointments: Cancelled appointments within a group must remain visible with a visual cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed to provide staff with operational context.
7. Standalone & Non-Grouped Behavior: Patients with single appointments or appointment types not associated with a multi-resource group must appear on the dashboard exactly as they do today with no grouping applied.
userStories.description: As a front desk staff member, I want to see all same-day appointments associated with a patient in a single grouped view on the practice dashboard, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, so that I can confirm paperwork completion and understand the full schedule at a glance before check-in.

userStories.summary: Smart Reminder Orchestration for Multi-Resource Same-Day Appointments
userStories.description: As a practice administrator configuring Yosi workflows in PageCMS, I want the reminder system to intelligently consolidate and sequence reminders when a patient has multiple same-day appointments, regardless of whether individual appointment types are configured with immediate-send or delayed cadences so that patients receive one coherent, timely communication about their visit day without duplicate or conflicting reminders, and practices do not have to sacrifice their immediate confirmation workflow to enable multi-resource grouping.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • When a multi-resource group is configured in PageCMS for specific appointment types, the system only applies consolidation logic to appointments of those types. Other same-day appointments for the same patient are processed independently. • PageCMS must allow practice administrators to define multi-resource groups at the appointment type level (e.g., 'Ultrasound ID 3 + New Patient ID 1 = Group A'). • A single appointment type can belong to only one multi-resource group per practice. • Appointment types not in any group continue to behave as standalone appointments with no change to existing logic. • The existing practice-wide multi-resource flag is deprecated once all practices are migrated to appointment-type-level configuration. • The first consolidated reminder is not sent until the configured hold window has elapsed after the earliest appointment in the group is booked. • PageCMS must allow the hold window to be configured in minutes, hours, or days per practice, with supported values including 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 calendar day, and 2 calendar days. • The default value for the hold window remains 1 calendar day for backward compatibility. • The hold window defines how long the system waits after the first appointment in a group is booked before sending the first reminder, to allow time for all associated appointments to be scheduled. • If all appointments in the group are booked before the hold window expires, the system will send the consolidated reminder immediately after the window closes without waiting for the full configured duration. • When immediate send is configured on an appointment type and the patient self-schedules via Yosi Scheduler, the immediate confirmation fires. No second immediate reminder fires when the associated appointment is subsequently booked by staff. • All subsequent reminders (MSG-2, MSG-3, and beyond) are sent only to the earliest appointment in the group and follow the consolidated cadence. • If staff books an earlier same-day appointment after the immediate send has already fired, and an 'appointment updated' template is configured for the practice in PageCMS, a notification is sent to the patient informing them of the earlier arrival time. This 'appointment updated' notification is a new configurable message type and is optional. • When the earliest appointment in a multi-resource group is cancelled, the system identifies the next-earliest active appointment in the group. • Subsequent reminders continue for the promoted appointment. • If a promotion notification template is configured, the patient is notified. • If no other active appointments remain in the group, the invite is closed and no further reminders are sent. • When multi-resource grouping is not enabled for a practice or appointment type, existing reminder behavior is completely unchanged.

userStories.summary: Route Intake Paperwork Submissions to the Correct Appointment Based on Appointment Type
userStories.description: As a clinical provider and front desk staff at an OBGYN practice, I want each section of the patient's intake paperwork to be associated with and submitted against the correct appointment ID based on which appointment type that form section belongs to so that when a patient checks in for their New Patient appointment, the provider sees the completed HPI, ROS, and clinical screeners against that encounter — not against the earlier Ultrasound appointment — and front desk staff can confirm completion status per appointment accurately.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • Each form section (page) in PageCMS must be associated with one or more appointment type IDs. • When a patient lands on the consolidated paperwork page, the system determines which form sections to display for each appointment based on this mapping. • When a patient submits a form section, the system routes the submission to the appointment ID whose appointment type matches the form section's PageCMS mapping. • When a patient submits demographics on the consolidated landing page, the demographics API call is made against all appointment IDs in the group whose appointment types are configured to receive demographics in PageCMS. • Demographics and other sections shared across multiple appointment types in the group are written to all relevant appointment IDs. • When a patient submits HPI, ROS, or clinical screeners, the submission is stored in Yosi DB against the appointment ID whose appointment type is configured for those sections — not against the earliest appointment ID. • Encounter-dependent sections are stored in Yosi DB with patient_id, practice_id, appointment_id (from appointment type mapping), and encounter_id = null until check-in. • The appointment note 'patient has completed intake' is written to each appointment in the group separately via the correct appointment ID. • When the Athena check-in trigger fires and an encounter ID is received, the system matches it against the stored appointment_id and pushes the data. • If the encounter ID arrives for the New Patient appointment (10 AM), encounter-dependent data stored against the New Patient appointment_id is pushed, while data stored against the Ultrasound appointment_id (e.g., demographics) is unaffected. • If an encounter ID arrives for an appointment that has no encounter-dependent data stored (e.g., Ultrasound), the system takes no action for those sections. • In the case where an appointment outside the group will occur on the same day as a group, form sections for the outside-appointment will be updated to their respective appointment (existing behavior). • For practices not using multi-resource grouping, form submission routing is completely unchanged.

userStories.summary: Consolidated Same-Day Appointment View on Patient Landing Page
userStories.description: As a patient with multiple same-day appointments at an OBGYN practice, I want a single link in my reminder to show me all of my appointments for that day and the relevant paperwork for each, clearly organised so I know what to complete for which visit so that I can complete all required paperwork in one session without confusion about which forms belong to which appointment, and I understand the full picture of my visit day including the correct arrival time.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • A new endpoint GET /patient/appointments/same-day?token={invite_token} must return all active appointments for the patient on the same calendar date that belong to the same multi-resource group. • Cancelled or rescheduled appointments are excluded from the response of the API call. • Appointments on different days are never included regardless of patient or practice. • If the sibling lookup returns only one appointment (single-appointment patient or non-grouped type), the landing page renders as today with no change to the existing experience. • When a patient with two same-day grouped appointments clicks the reminder link, the landing page displays both appointments in chronological order with their time, type, and provider. • When the sibling lookup returns multiple appointments, the landing page renders a consolidated view showing all same-day appointments in chronological order, earliest first. • Each appointment is clearly labelled with its time and action button. • The earliest appointment is visually distinguished as the primary arrival appointment (e.g., 'Please arrive for this appointment first'). • Form sections are grouped under their respective appointment. The patient completes paperwork for each appointment in sequence within one session. • Form sections displayed under each appointment match the PageCMS appointment type configuration for that appointment type. • Shared sections (e.g., demographics) that apply to multiple appointments are shown once and submitted to all relevant appointments — the patient is not asked to re-enter the same information twice. • The page uses the PageCMS configuration of the earliest appointment as the base styling and branding, with appointment-type-specific content (instructions, provider notes) rendered per section. • If one appointment in the group is cancelled after the reminder is sent, the cancelled appointment does not appear on the landing page when the patient clicks the link. • If the sibling lookup API call fails or times out, the patient sees only the single appointment from the link token, with no error message displayed. • If all appointments in the group are cancelled by the time the patient clicks the link, the page displays an appropriate message directing the patient to contact the practice. • The link remains valid and shows the current state of appointments at the time of access — it is not a static snapshot. • For patients with appointments on different days, the landing page shows only the appointment matching the token date, with no other-day appointments appearing. • For single-appointment patients or appointment types not in a multi-resource group, the landing page renders identically to today's experience.

userStories.summary: Show Associated Same-Day Appointments and Consolidated Paperwork Status on Practice Dashboard
userStories.description: As a front desk staff member at an OBGYN practice using the Yosi dashboard, I want to see all same-day appointments associated to a patient in a single grouped view, with a combined paperwork completion indicator, and the ability to click through to each appointment's detail so that I can confirm at a glance that a patient has completed all required paperwork before check-in, understand the full schedule for that patient's visit day, and take action on any individual appointment without switching views.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: • On both today's dashboard view and future date views, appointments belonging to the same multi-resource group are displayed as a grouped unit anchored to the earliest appointment. • When a patient has two same-day appointments in a multi-resource group, the dashboard shows them as a grouped unit with the earliest appointment as the primary row and the later appointment visually associated beneath it. • The earliest appointment is the primary row, and associated appointments are visually nested beneath it. • Each associated appointment shows: appointment time, appointment type, provider name, and individual paperwork completion status. • The group as a whole shows a combined paperwork status indicator: All Complete, Partially Complete, or Not Started. • The combined paperwork status shows 'All Complete' only when all form sections across all appointments in the group have been submitted. • The combined paperwork status shows 'Partially Complete' when at least one form section has been submitted but at least one required section remains incomplete across any appointment in the group. • The combined paperwork status shows 'Not Started' when no form sections have been submitted for any appointment in the group. • The paperwork completion status on the dashboard accurately reflects the corrected per-appointment routing from Story 2 (e.g., Ultrasound shows its own completion, New Patient shows its own completion). • Clicking any appointment in the group (earliest or associated) opens the existing appointment detail view for that specific appointment. • All existing actions available in the appointment detail view (e.g., view paperwork, send manual reminder, view patient profile) are available for associated appointments. • There is no change to the appointment detail view itself in this story. • The grouping is based on the appointment date being viewed; a patient with appointments on different days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday) does not have those grouped together. • A cancelled appointment within a group remains visible on the dashboard with a cancelled indicator until the appointment date has passed, to give staff context. • Patients with a single appointment or with appointment types not in a multi-resource group appear on the dashboard exactly as today, with no grouping applied.

requests.expectedResults: The API should respond with a 200 OK status code and a JSON array containing 100 post objects.
requests.name: Verify successful retrieval of all posts
requests.description: Send a GET request to the /posts endpoint to fetch all available posts.
Examine a few post objects in the response to ensure they adhere to the expected schema.
requests.name: Validate response structure and data types
requests.expectedResults: Each post object should contain 'userId' (number), 'id' (number), 'title' (string), and 'body' (string) fields. All fields must be present and have the correct data types.
All 'id' fields across the 100 posts must be unique integers.
requests.name: Verify unique post IDs
requests.description: Check all 'id' values in the response array to ensure their uniqueness.
Iterate through the posts and verify that the 'title' and 'body' fields are not empty strings.
requests.name: Verify non-empty title and body content
requests.expectedResults: The 'title' and 'body' fields for all posts should contain non-empty string values.

requests.description: Check the range and validity of 'userId' and 'id' fields.
requests.name: Verify numerical integrity of userId and id fields
requests.expectedResults: 'userId' and 'id' fields should be positive integers. 'id' should range from 1 to 100, and 'userId' should range from 1 to 10, sequentially assigned to groups of posts.
The posts should be ordered by their 'id' field in ascending numerical order.
requests.name: Verify response array order
requests.description: Check if the posts are returned in a specific order, e.g., by 'id'.
Attempt to use an unsupported HTTP method (e.g., POST, PUT, DELETE) on the /posts endpoint.

requests.expectedResults: The API should respond with a 405 Method Not Allowed status code or a similar error indicating the method is not supported for this endpoint.
The response should include appropriate headers such as 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' and 'Content-Length'.
requests.description: Check for expected and relevant headers in the successful response.
requests.name: Verify response headers
Create Cart with Valid User, Date, and Products
requests.description: Send a POST request to the /carts endpoint with a correctly formatted JSON body containing a valid userId, a future date, and an array of products, each with a valid productId and quantity.
requests.expectedResults: HTTP 201 Created response. The response body should contain the newly created cart object, including an 'id', the provided 'userId', 'date', and 'products'.
HTTP 400 Bad Request error. The response body should clearly indicate a JSON parsing issue or an invalid request format. (This directly addresses the observed 'Bad Request' HTML response).

Send a POST request to the /carts endpoint with an entirely empty request body.
requests.name: Attempt Cart Creation with Empty Request Body
requests.expectedResults: HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity, with an error message indicating that required fields are missing.

requests.expectedResults: HTTP 201 Created response with the cart successfully created but containing no products, or an HTTP 400 Bad Request if the API requires at least one product.

userStories.description:
User-provided requirements text used to generate user stories:

The system should allow authorized users to add, edit, view, and update disability information for an individual. The disability details should be stored securely and associated with the person's profile.

Business Rules
Disability type must be selected from a configurable master list.
Multiple disability records may be allowed based on business requirements.
Disability percentage must be between 0 and 100.
Certificate expiry date cannot be earlier than the issue date.
Future issue dates are not allowed.
Audit history must be maintained for all changes.
Access to disability information should be role-based.

Additional Context / Guidelines:
No additional context provided.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Original requirements used for Gemini User Story generation.

userStories.description:
User-provided requirements text used to generate user stories:

1.	Added a new field “Person with Disability” which represents whether a person is disabled or not. Enable it, if the person is disabled.
2.	If “Person with Disability” is enabled then “Disability Details” will appear and details of the disability should be filled in this.
a.	Click on “+ add new” to enter disability details
b.	All three properties - “Disability Percentage”, “Disability Types”, “Disability Certificates” are mandatory if “Person with Disability” is enabled.

Person with Disability” field is required when creating a new person.
2.	Valid Disability percentage (0-100), certificate and at least one disability type are required when 'Person with Disability' is 'True'.
3.	Disability percentage, certificate and disability type must not be set when 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or not set.

Additional Context / Guidelines:
No additional context provided.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Original requirements used for Gemini User Story generation.

GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'No' or unchecked WHEN viewing the person form THEN the 'Disability Details' section is not visible.GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'Yes' or checked WHEN viewing the person form THEN the 'Disability Details' section is clearly visible, containing controls to add disability entries.
userStories.description: As an administrator managing a person record, I want the 'Disability Details' section to appear only when 'Person with Disability' is marked as 'Yes' so that I can provide specific disability information only when relevant.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN the 'Disability Details' section is visible (i.e., 'Person with Disability' is 'Yes') WHEN a '+ Add New' button (or similar control) is clicked within the 'Disability Details' section THEN a new set of input fields for 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', and 'Disability Certificates' appears, allowing for entry of a single disability. The system allows adding multiple such entries for different disabilities. Each disability entry can be individually edited or removed.
userStories.description: As an administrator, I want to be able to add multiple disability entries within the 'Disability Details' section so that I can capture comprehensive information for a person with multiple disabilities.
userStories.summary: Add and Manage Individual Disability Entries

userStories.description: As an administrator, I want the 'Person with Disability' field to be required when creating a new person so that an explicit decision about a person's disability status is made at the time of record creation.
userStories.summary: Enforce Mandatory 'Person with Disability' Field for New Records
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN a user is creating a new person record WHEN the 'Person with Disability' field is left unset/unanswered AND the user attempts to save the record THEN an error message is displayed, indicating that the 'Person with Disability' field is mandatory. The system prevents saving the new person record until this field is answered (Yes/No).

userStories.summary: Validate Mandatory and Valid Disability Details when 'Person with Disability' is 'True'
userStories.description: As an administrator, I want the system to validate the 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', and 'Disability Certificates' fields for each disability entry so that only complete and accurate disability information is saved when 'Person with Disability' is 'Yes'.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN 'Person with Disability' is 'Yes' and at least one disability entry is present. WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is left empty for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating 'Disability Percentage' is required. WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is entered outside the range of 0-100 (e.g., -1, 101) for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating 'Disability Percentage must be between 0 and 100'. WHEN no 'Disability Type' is selected/provided for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating that at least one 'Disability Type' is required. WHEN no 'Disability Certificate' is provided for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating 'Disability Certificate' is required. WHEN all mandatory fields for all disability entries ('Disability Percentage' (0-100), at least one 'Disability Type', 'Disability Certificate') are valid and present THEN the system allows the person record to be saved (assuming other validations pass).

GIVEN a user is creating or editing a person record. WHEN 'Person with Disability' is set to 'No' or is left unset. AND there are values entered or existing in 'Disability Details' fields (Percentage, Types, Certificates). WHEN the user attempts to save the record THEN the system automatically clears any 'Disability Details' and proceeds with saving the record without an error. Alternatively, the system displays an error message preventing saving and requires that 'Disability Details' fields must be empty or cleared before saving.
userStories.summary: Prevent Saving Disability Details when 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or Unset
userStories.description: As an administrator, I want the system to prevent or clear any 'Disability Details' from being saved if 'Person with Disability' is marked as 'No' or is unset so that data consistency is maintained and irrelevant information is not stored.

a.	Click on “+ add new” to enter disability details
b.	All three properties - “Disability Percentage”, “Disability Types”, “Disability Certificates” are mandatory if “Person with Disability” is enabled.

2.	Valid Disability percentage (0-100), certificate and at least one disability type are required when 'Person with Disability' is 'True'.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Original requirements used for Gemini User Story generation.

The 'Person with Disability' field must be visible on both the new person creation form and the person edit form.When creating a new person, the 'Person with Disability' field must be marked as mandatory.The system must prevent saving a new person record if the 'Person with Disability' field is not set.
userStories.description: As a user creating or editing a person record, I want the 'Person with Disability' field to be consistently displayed and enforced as required during new person creation, so that I can accurately and mandatorily specify a person's disability status.
userStories.summary: Manage 'Person with Disability' Field Visibility and Requirement

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'False' or not enabled, THEN the 'Disability Details' section must be hidden.GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'True' or enabled, THEN the 'Disability Details' section must become visible.The 'Disability Details' section must include a '+ add new' button or link, allowing the user to create new disability detail entries.
userStories.summary: Conditional Display and Interaction for Disability Details Section
userStories.description: As a user managing a person's record, I want the 'Disability Details' section to dynamically appear and allow adding entries only when 'Person with Disability' is enabled, so that I can efficiently enter relevant disability information when applicable.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN 'Person with Disability' is 'True' and a user is adding/editing a disability detail entry,WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is empty or not provided,THEN the system must display a validation error and prevent saving.WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is less than 0 or greater than 100,THEN the system must display a validation error (e.g., 'Disability percentage must be between 0 and 100') and prevent saving.WHEN 'Disability Types' has no types selected/provided,THEN the system must display a validation error (e.g., 'At least one Disability Type is required') and prevent saving.WHEN 'Disability Certificates' is empty or not provided,THEN the system must display a validation error and prevent saving.GIVEN 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or not enabled,WHEN any values are attempted to be saved for 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', or 'Disability Certificates',THEN the system must prevent these values from being saved or automatically clear them upon saving to ensure data integrity.
userStories.summary: Validate and Enforce Mandatory Disability Details Fields
userStories.description: As a user entering disability information for a person, I want the system to validate and enforce all required properties within the 'Disability Details' section, and ensure data consistency based on the 'Person with Disability' status, so that complete and accurate disability records are maintained.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Original requirements used for Gemini User Story generation.

userStories.description: As a system user, I want to be able to indicate if a person is disabled or not during their creation or edit, so that we can capture essential demographic information for compliance with RBI and SC directions and enable inclusive finance.
userStories.summary: Capture 'Person with Disability' status during creation/edit
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given a user is creating or editing a person record,Then the 'Person with Disability' field must be visible and available for selection.And the 'Person with Disability' field must be required when creating a new person.And the field should allow selecting 'True' (person is disabled) or 'False' (person is not disabled).

Given 'Person with Disability' is set to 'True',When the user interacts with the form,Then a 'Disability Details' section must appear, revealing fields for 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', and 'Disability Certificates'.And all three fields ('Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', 'Disability Certificates') must be mandatory.And the 'Disability Percentage' field must accept numeric values between 0 and 100, inclusive.And the 'Disability Types' field must allow selection/entry of at least one disability type.And the 'Disability Certificates' field must allow uploading of a disability certificate image.
userStories.description: As a system user, I want to capture specific details about a person's disability, including percentage, types, and supporting certificates, when they are identified as disabled, so that we have comprehensive and verifiable data for compliance and downstream processes.
userStories.summary: Capture detailed disability information when 'Person with Disability' is true

userStories.description: As a system, I want to enforce strict validation rules on disability related fields during person creation or edit, so that data integrity is maintained and compliance requirements are met.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given 'Person with Disability' is 'True',When the user attempts to save the person record,Then the system must validate that:    'Disability Percentage' is between 0 and 100 (inclusive).    At least one 'Disability Type' is provided.    A 'Disability Certificate' is uploaded.    If any of these conditions are not met, an appropriate error message must be displayed, and the save action prevented.Given 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or not set,When the user attempts to save the person record,Then the system must validate that:    'Disability Percentage' is not set/empty.    'Disability Types' is not set/empty.    'Disability Certificates' is not set/empty.    If any of these conditions are not met (i.e., disability details are provided when not disabled), an appropriate error message must be displayed, and the save action prevented.

userStories.description: As a loan officer, I want a new manual verification step to confirm the primary applicant's disability percentage matches their uploaded certificate, so that we ensure accuracy and compliance for loans involving disabled individuals.
userStories.summary: Introduce manual verification for disability percentage on loans
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given a loan application has a primary applicant with 'Person with Disability' set to 'True',Then a new manual verification step titled 'Disability percentage matches certificate' must be added to the loan workflow.And this verification step must provide access to the uploaded disability certificate and the entered disability percentage.And the loan officer must be able to manually update the status of this verification step to 'Verified' or 'Rejected'.And the status of this verification must be auditable.

userStories.summary: Introduce manual verification for disability type on loans
userStories.description: As a loan officer, I want a new manual verification step to confirm the primary applicant's disability types match their uploaded certificate, so that we ensure accuracy and compliance for loans involving disabled individuals.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given a loan application has a primary applicant with 'Person with Disability' set to 'True',Then a new manual verification step titled 'Disability type matches certificate' must be added to the loan workflow.And this verification step must provide access to the uploaded disability certificate and the entered disability types.And the loan officer must be able to manually update the status of this verification step to 'Verified' or 'Rejected'.And the status of this verification must be auditable.

Given a loan involves a primary applicant, guarantor, or co-borrower where 'Person with Disability' is 'True',When the individual proceeds to the E-signing process,Then all available Aadhar E-sign options must be presented to them without restriction.And this functionality must apply irrespective of any other factors that might typically restrict E-sign options.
userStories.description: As a system, I want to ensure all available Aadhar E-sign options are presented to primary applicants, guarantors, or co-borrowers who are identified as disabled, so that we provide inclusive financial services as directed by RBI and SC.
userStories.summary: Enable all Aadhar E-sign options for disabled loan applicants/guarantors/co-borrowers

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: The variable 'IsDisabled' must be exposed, populating with 'Yes' if the primary applicant's 'Person with Disability' is 'True', 'No' if 'False', and 'NA' if not set/applicable.The variable 'DisabilityPercentage' must be exposed, populating with the numeric percentage value if available, otherwise 'NA'.The variable 'DisabilityTypes' must be exposed, populating with comma-separated disability type names if available, otherwise 'NA'.The variable 'DisabilityCertificate' must be exposed, populating with the uploaded certificate images (references/data) if available, otherwise 'NA'.These exposed variables must be accessible and usable by the document generation engine to populate dynamic fields.
userStories.description: As a system, I want to expose key disability-related variables for the primary applicant of a loan within document controls, so that downstream documents and processes can be systematically designed and generated with accurate and compliant information.
userStories.summary: Expose disability-related data in document controls for downstream use

userStories.description: As a system, I want to ensure that only image files are accepted for disability certificate uploads, so that we maintain data integrity, adhere to document type requirements, and simplify downstream processing of these documents.
userStories.summary: Restrict disability certificate uploads to image files only
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: When a user attempts to upload a 'Disability Certificate',Then the system must only accept common image file formats (e.g., JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP) and PDF files that contain embedded images.If a non-image/non-image-embedded PDF file type (e.g., DOCX, XLSX, TXT) is selected for upload, an appropriate error message must be displayed, and the upload must be prevented.The file upload interface should ideally filter available file types to images during selection.

import { Page, Locator, expect } from '@playwright/test';/** * BasePage provides common methods and properties for all Page Objects. */export abstract class BasePage {  readonly page: Page;  constructor(page: Page) {    this.page = page;  }  /**   * Navigates to a specified URL.   * @param url The URL to navigate to.   */  async navigate(url: string) {    await this.page.goto(url);  }  /**   * Clicks on an element identified by a locator.   * @param locator The Playwright Locator for the element.   */  async clickElement(locator: Locator) {    await locator.click();  }  /**   * Fills text into an input field identified by a locator.   * @param locator The Playwright Locator for the input field.   * @param text The text to fill into the input.   */  async fillElement(locator: Locator, text: string) {    await locator.fill(text);  }  /**   * Asserts that the current URL matches a given regular expression.   * @param urlRegex A regular expression to match against the current URL.   * @param timeout Optional timeout for the assertion in milliseconds.   */  async expectUrl(urlRegex: RegExp, timeout?: number) {    await expect(this.page).toHaveURL(urlRegex, { timeout });  }  /**   * Asserts that an element identified by a locator is visible.   * @param locator The Playwright Locator for the element.   * @param timeout Optional timeout for the assertion in milliseconds.   */  async expectElementToBeVisible(locator: Locator, timeout?: number) {    await expect(locator).toBeVisible({ timeout });  }  /**   * Asserts that an element contains a specific text.   * @param locator The Playwright Locator for the element.   * @param text The expected text content.   * @param timeout Optional timeout for the assertion in milliseconds.   */  async expectElementToContainText(locator: Locator, text: string, timeout?: number) {    await expect(locator).toContainText(text, { timeout });  }}

import { Locator, Page } from '@playwright/test';import { BasePage } from './BasePage';/** * MainPage represents the main application interface where login, navigation, * and report access actions occur. */export class MainPage extends BasePage {  // Locators  readonly userIdInput: Locator;  readonly passwordInput: Locator;  readonly loginButton: Locator;  readonly masterMenuLink: Locator;  readonly userMenuItem: Locator;  readonly reportsMenuLink: Locator;  readonly leadTimeReportMenuItem: Locator;  constructor(page: Page) {    super(page);    this.userIdInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'User ID' });    this.passwordInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' });    this.loginButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Login' });    this.masterMenuLink = page.getByText('Master ▸');    this.userMenuItem = page.getByText('User');    this.reportsMenuLink = page.getByText('Reports ▸');    this.leadTimeReportMenuItem = page.getByText('Lead Time Report');  }  /**   * Navigates directly to the login page.   * @param path Optional path to append to the base URL, defaults to '/#/login'.   */  async gotoLoginPage(path: string = '/#/login') {    await this.navigate(path);    console.log(`Navigated to login page: ${this.page.url()}`);  }  /**   * Performs user login with provided credentials.   * @param username The username to enter.   * @param password The password to enter.   */  async login(username: string, password: string) {    await this.fillElement(this.userIdInput, username);    await this.fillElement(this.passwordInput, password);    await this.clickElement(this.loginButton);    console.log(`Attempted login with user: ${username}`);  }  /**   * Navigates to the User Management page via the 'Master' menu.   */  async navigateToUserPage() {    await this.clickElement(this.masterMenuLink);    await this.clickElement(this.userMenuItem);    console.log('Navigated to User page.');  }  /**   * Navigates to the Lead Time Report page via the 'Reports' menu.   */  async navigateToLeadTimeReportPage() {    await this.clickElement(this.reportsMenuLink);    await this.clickElement(this.leadTimeReportMenuItem);    console.log('Navigated to Lead Time Report page.');  }}

import { Page, Locator, expect } from '@playwright/test';export abstract class BasePage {  protected readonly page: Page;  constructor(page: Page) {    this.page = page;  }  async navigate(url: string): Promise<void> {    await this.page.goto(url);  }  async click(locator: Locator, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await locator.click(options);  }  async fill(locator: Locator, value: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await locator.fill(value, options);  }  async check(locator: Locator, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await locator.check(options);  }  async scroll(locator: Locator, x: number, y: number): Promise<void> {    await locator.evaluate((element, coords) => {      element.scrollTo(coords.x, coords.y);    }, { x, y });  }  async assertUrl(expectedUrl: string | RegExp, message?: string): Promise<void> {    await expect(this.page, message || `Expected URL to be ${expectedUrl}`).toHaveURL(expectedUrl);  }  async assertElementVisibility(locator: Locator, message?: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await expect(locator, message || `Expected element to be visible`).toBeVisible(options);  }  async assertElementText(locator: Locator, expectedText: string, message?: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await expect(locator, message || `Expected element to have text: ${expectedText}`).toHaveText(expectedText, options);  }  async assertElementIsChecked(locator: Locator, message?: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await expect(locator, message || `Expected element to be checked`).toBeChecked(options);  }}

import { Page, Locator } from '@playwright/test';import { BasePage } from './BasePage';export class MainPage extends BasePage {  // Locators  private readonly signUpButton: Locator;  private readonly mobileNumberInput: Locator;  private readonly termsCheckbox: Locator;  private readonly continueButton: Locator;  private readonly otpVerificationText: Locator;  private readonly otpInputs: Locator; // Represents all 6 OTP input fields  private readonly confirmOtpButton: Locator;  private readonly viewMoreSportsButton: Locator;  private readonly exploreSportsCategoriesText: Locator;  private readonly viewMoreCentresButton: Locator;  private readonly addToWishlistButton: Locator;  private readonly removeFromWishlistButton: Locator;  private readonly pauseVideoButton: Locator;  private readonly playVideoButton: Locator;  constructor(page: Page) {    super(page);    // Initialize locators    this.signUpButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Sign Up' });    this.mobileNumberInput = page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Enter the Mobile Number' });    this.termsCheckbox = page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'on' });    this.continueButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' });    this.otpVerificationText = page.getByText('Please enter OTP');    // OTP inputs are dynamic, using a general selector and then nth()    this.otpInputs = page.locator('#root > div > div > div > div > div:nth-of-type(3) > input');    this.confirmOtpButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm' });    this.viewMoreSportsButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'VIEW MORE SPORTS' });    this.exploreSportsCategoriesText = page.getByText('Explore our sports categories');    this.viewMoreCentresButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'VIEW MORE CENTRES' });    this.addToWishlistButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to wishlist' });    this.removeFromWishlistButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Remove from wishlist' });    this.pauseVideoButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pause video' });    this.playVideoButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Play video' });  }  // Actions  async navigateToAboutUs(): Promise<void> {    await this.navigate('/about-us');    await this.assertUrl('https://www.machaxi.com/about-us', 'About Us page URL is incorrect');  }  async startUserRegistration(mobileNumber: string): Promise<void> {    await this.click(this.signUpButton);    await this.assertElementVisibility(this.mobileNumberInput, 'Mobile number input field not visible after clicking Sign Up');    await this.fill(this.mobileNumberInput, mobileNumber);    await this.check(this.termsCheckbox);    await this.click(this.continueButton);    await this.assertElementVisibility(this.otpVerificationText, 'OTP verification screen did not appear.');  }  async enterOtp(otp: string): Promise<void> {    if (otp.length !== 6) {      throw new Error('OTP must be 6 digits long.');    }    for (let i = 0; i < otp.length; i++) {      const digitLocator = this.otpInputs.nth(i);      await this.fill(digitLocator, otp[i]);    }  }  async confirmOtp(): Promise<void> {    await this.click(this.confirmOtpButton);    await this.assertUrl(/.*dashboard|home/, 'User not redirected to dashboard/home page after OTP confirmation');  }  async viewMoreSports(): Promise<void> {    await this.click(this.viewMoreSportsButton);    await this.assertElementVisibility(this.exploreSportsCategoriesText, 'Sports categories content not visible');  }  async viewMoreCentres(): Promise<void> {    await this.click(this.viewMoreCentresButton);    await this.assertUrl(/.*centres/, 'Did not navigate to centres page');  }  async navigateToGetMachaxiAppPage(): Promise<void> {    await this.navigate('https://machaxi.app.link/get-machaxi');    await this.assertUrl(/.*get-machaxi/, 'Get Machaxi app page URL is incorrect');  }  async navigateToPlayStore(appUrl: string): Promise<void> {    await this.navigate(appUrl);    await this.assertUrl(/.*play.google.com/, 'Did not navigate to Play Store URL');  }  async addToWishlist(): Promise<void> {    await this.click(this.addToWishlistButton);    await this.assertElementVisibility(this.removeFromWishlistButton, 'Remove from wishlist button not visible, item not added to wishlist');  }  async assertVideoPaused(): Promise<void> {    await this.click(this.pauseVideoButton);    await this.assertElementVisibility(this.playVideoButton, 'Play video button not visible, video might not have paused.');  }  async scrollBodyTo(x: number, y: number): Promise<void> {    await this.scroll(this.page.locator('html > body'), x, y);  }}

userStories.description:
User-provided requirements text used to generate user stories:

The system should allow authorized users to add, edit, view, and update disability information for an individual. The disability details should be stored securely and associated with the person's profile.

Business Rules
Disability type must be selected from a configurable master list.
Multiple disability records may be allowed based on business requirements.
Disability percentage must be between 0 and 100.
Certificate expiry date cannot be earlier than the issue date.
Future issue dates are not allowed.
Audit history must be maintained for all changes.
Access to disability information should be role-based.

No additional context provided.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Original requirements used for Gemini User Story generation.

GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'No' or unchecked WHEN viewing the person form THEN the 'Disability Details' section is not visible.GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'Yes' or checked WHEN viewing the person form THEN the 'Disability Details' section is clearly visible, containing controls to add disability entries.
userStories.description: As an administrator managing a person record, I want the 'Disability Details' section to appear only when 'Person with Disability' is marked as 'Yes' so that I can provide specific disability information only when relevant.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN the 'Disability Details' section is visible (i.e., 'Person with Disability' is 'Yes') WHEN a '+ Add New' button (or similar control) is clicked within the 'Disability Details' section THEN a new set of input fields for 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', and 'Disability Certificates' appears, allowing for entry of a single disability. The system allows adding multiple such entries for different disabilities. Each disability entry can be individually edited or removed.
userStories.description: As an administrator, I want to be able to add multiple disability entries within the 'Disability Details' section so that I can capture comprehensive information for a person with multiple disabilities.
userStories.summary: Add and Manage Individual Disability Entries

userStories.description: As an administrator, I want the 'Person with Disability' field to be required when creating a new person so that an explicit decision about a person's disability status is made at the time of record creation.
userStories.summary: Enforce Mandatory 'Person with Disability' Field for New Records
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN a user is creating a new person record WHEN the 'Person with Disability' field is left unset/unanswered AND the user attempts to save the record THEN an error message is displayed, indicating that the 'Person with Disability' field is mandatory. The system prevents saving the new person record until this field is answered (Yes/No).

userStories.summary: Validate Mandatory and Valid Disability Details when 'Person with Disability' is 'True'
userStories.description: As an administrator, I want the system to validate the 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', and 'Disability Certificates' fields for each disability entry so that only complete and accurate disability information is saved when 'Person with Disability' is 'Yes'.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN 'Person with Disability' is 'Yes' and at least one disability entry is present. WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is left empty for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating 'Disability Percentage' is required. WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is entered outside the range of 0-100 (e.g., -1, 101) for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating 'Disability Percentage must be between 0 and 100'. WHEN no 'Disability Type' is selected/provided for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating that at least one 'Disability Type' is required. WHEN no 'Disability Certificate' is provided for any entry THEN an error message is displayed, indicating 'Disability Certificate' is required. WHEN all mandatory fields for all disability entries ('Disability Percentage' (0-100), at least one 'Disability Type', 'Disability Certificate') are valid and present THEN the system allows the person record to be saved (assuming other validations pass).

GIVEN a user is creating or editing a person record. WHEN 'Person with Disability' is set to 'No' or is left unset. AND there are values entered or existing in 'Disability Details' fields (Percentage, Types, Certificates). WHEN the user attempts to save the record THEN the system automatically clears any 'Disability Details' and proceeds with saving the record without an error. Alternatively, the system displays an error message preventing saving and requires that 'Disability Details' fields must be empty or cleared before saving.
userStories.summary: Prevent Saving Disability Details when 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or Unset
userStories.description: As an administrator, I want the system to prevent or clear any 'Disability Details' from being saved if 'Person with Disability' is marked as 'No' or is unset so that data consistency is maintained and irrelevant information is not stored.

userStories.description: As a user creating or editing a person record, I want the 'Person with Disability' field to be consistently displayed and enforced as required during new person creation, so that I can accurately and mandatorily specify a person's disability status.
userStories.summary: Manage 'Person with Disability' Field Visibility and Requirement

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'False' or not enabled, THEN the 'Disability Details' section must be hidden.GIVEN the 'Person with Disability' field is set to 'True' or enabled, THEN the 'Disability Details' section must become visible.The 'Disability Details' section must include a '+ add new' button or link, allowing the user to create new disability detail entries.
userStories.summary: Conditional Display and Interaction for Disability Details Section
userStories.description: As a user managing a person's record, I want the 'Disability Details' section to dynamically appear and allow adding entries only when 'Person with Disability' is enabled, so that I can efficiently enter relevant disability information when applicable.

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: GIVEN 'Person with Disability' is 'True' and a user is adding/editing a disability detail entry,WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is empty or not provided,THEN the system must display a validation error and prevent saving.WHEN 'Disability Percentage' is less than 0 or greater than 100,THEN the system must display a validation error (e.g., 'Disability percentage must be between 0 and 100') and prevent saving.WHEN 'Disability Types' has no types selected/provided,THEN the system must display a validation error (e.g., 'At least one Disability Type is required') and prevent saving.WHEN 'Disability Certificates' is empty or not provided,THEN the system must display a validation error and prevent saving.GIVEN 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or not enabled,WHEN any values are attempted to be saved for 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', or 'Disability Certificates',THEN the system must prevent these values from being saved or automatically clear them upon saving to ensure data integrity.

userStories.description: As a user entering disability information for a person, I want the system to validate and enforce all required properties within the 'Disability Details' section, and ensure data consistency based on the 'Person with Disability' status, so that complete and accurate disability records are maintained.

userStories.description: As a system user, I want to be able to indicate if a person is disabled or not during their creation or edit, so that we can capture essential demographic information for compliance with RBI and SC directions and enable inclusive finance.
userStories.summary: Capture 'Person with Disability' status during creation/edit
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given a user is creating or editing a person record,Then the 'Person with Disability' field must be visible and available for selection.And the 'Person with Disability' field must be required when creating a new person.And the field should allow selecting 'True' (person is disabled) or 'False' (person is not disabled).

Given 'Person with Disability' is set to 'True',When the user interacts with the form,Then a 'Disability Details' section must appear, revealing fields for 'Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', and 'Disability Certificates'.And all three fields ('Disability Percentage', 'Disability Types', 'Disability Certificates') must be mandatory.And the 'Disability Percentage' field must accept numeric values between 0 and 100, inclusive.And the 'Disability Types' field must allow selection/entry of at least one disability type.And the 'Disability Certificates' field must allow uploading of a disability certificate image.
userStories.description: As a system user, I want to capture specific details about a person's disability, including percentage, types, and supporting certificates, when they are identified as disabled, so that we have comprehensive and verifiable data for compliance and downstream processes.
userStories.summary: Capture detailed disability information when 'Person with Disability' is true

userStories.description: As a system, I want to enforce strict validation rules on disability related fields during person creation or edit, so that data integrity is maintained and compliance requirements are met.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given 'Person with Disability' is 'True',When the user attempts to save the person record,Then the system must validate that:    'Disability Percentage' is between 0 and 100 (inclusive).    At least one 'Disability Type' is provided.    A 'Disability Certificate' is uploaded.    If any of these conditions are not met, an appropriate error message must be displayed, and the save action prevented.Given 'Person with Disability' is 'False' or not set,When the user attempts to save the person record,Then the system must validate that:    'Disability Percentage' is not set/empty.    'Disability Types' is not set/empty.    'Disability Certificates' is not set/empty.    If any of these conditions are not met (i.e., disability details are provided when not disabled), an appropriate error message must be displayed, and the save action prevented.

userStories.description: As a loan officer, I want a new manual verification step to confirm the primary applicant's disability percentage matches their uploaded certificate, so that we ensure accuracy and compliance for loans involving disabled individuals.
userStories.summary: Introduce manual verification for disability percentage on loans
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given a loan application has a primary applicant with 'Person with Disability' set to 'True',Then a new manual verification step titled 'Disability percentage matches certificate' must be added to the loan workflow.And this verification step must provide access to the uploaded disability certificate and the entered disability percentage.And the loan officer must be able to manually update the status of this verification step to 'Verified' or 'Rejected'.And the status of this verification must be auditable.

userStories.summary: Introduce manual verification for disability type on loans
userStories.description: As a loan officer, I want a new manual verification step to confirm the primary applicant's disability types match their uploaded certificate, so that we ensure accuracy and compliance for loans involving disabled individuals.
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: Given a loan application has a primary applicant with 'Person with Disability' set to 'True',Then a new manual verification step titled 'Disability type matches certificate' must be added to the loan workflow.And this verification step must provide access to the uploaded disability certificate and the entered disability types.And the loan officer must be able to manually update the status of this verification step to 'Verified' or 'Rejected'.And the status of this verification must be auditable.

Given a loan involves a primary applicant, guarantor, or co-borrower where 'Person with Disability' is 'True',When the individual proceeds to the E-signing process,Then all available Aadhar E-sign options must be presented to them without restriction.And this functionality must apply irrespective of any other factors that might typically restrict E-sign options.
userStories.description: As a system, I want to ensure all available Aadhar E-sign options are presented to primary applicants, guarantors, or co-borrowers who are identified as disabled, so that we provide inclusive financial services as directed by RBI and SC.
userStories.summary: Enable all Aadhar E-sign options for disabled loan applicants/guarantors/co-borrowers

userStories.acceptanceCriteria: The variable 'IsDisabled' must be exposed, populating with 'Yes' if the primary applicant's 'Person with Disability' is 'True', 'No' if 'False', and 'NA' if not set/applicable.The variable 'DisabilityPercentage' must be exposed, populating with the numeric percentage value if available, otherwise 'NA'.The variable 'DisabilityTypes' must be exposed, populating with comma-separated disability type names if available, otherwise 'NA'.The variable 'DisabilityCertificate' must be exposed, populating with the uploaded certificate images (references/data) if available, otherwise 'NA'.These exposed variables must be accessible and usable by the document generation engine to populate dynamic fields.
userStories.description: As a system, I want to expose key disability-related variables for the primary applicant of a loan within document controls, so that downstream documents and processes can be systematically designed and generated with accurate and compliant information.
userStories.summary: Expose disability-related data in document controls for downstream use

userStories.description: As a system, I want to ensure that only image files are accepted for disability certificate uploads, so that we maintain data integrity, adhere to document type requirements, and simplify downstream processing of these documents.
userStories.summary: Restrict disability certificate uploads to image files only
userStories.acceptanceCriteria: When a user attempts to upload a 'Disability Certificate',Then the system must only accept common image file formats (e.g., JPG, JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP) and PDF files that contain embedded images.If a non-image/non-image-embedded PDF file type (e.g., DOCX, XLSX, TXT) is selected for upload, an appropriate error message must be displayed, and the upload must be prevented.The file upload interface should ideally filter available file types to images during selection.

scenarios.description:
User Story: Add a new disability record to an individual's profile
Description:
As an Authorized User, I want to add new disability information for an individual so that their complete profile is accurately maintained.
Acceptance Criteria:
Given I am an Authorized User with appropriate permissions
When I navigate to an individual's profile and choose to add disability information
Then I should be able to select a disability type from a configurable master list
And I should be able to enter a disability percentage between 0 and 100
And I should be able to enter a certificate issue date that is not in the future
And I should be able to enter a certificate expiry date that is not earlier than the issue date
And the system should securely store the new disability record associated with the individual's profile
And an audit history entry should be created for the addition of the new record
And if any required field is missing or invalid, an appropriate error message should be displayed

Note: In a real scenario, this OTP would be dynamic      // and fetched from a test data source, email, or SMS service.      // For demonstration, we use the hardcoded OTP from the flow.      await mainPage.enterOtp('728555');      // Step: cw4bt - Click Confirm      // Step: cw4bt_assert_login_success - Assert redirection to dashboard/home      await mainPage.confirmOtp();    });    // ---- App Discovery Flow ----    await test.step('Discover Sports Categories', async () => {      // Step: dp8ipe - Scroll body      await mainPage.scrollBodyTo(0, 888);      // Step: uwk8re - Click VIEW MORE SPORTS      // Step: uwk8re_assert_sports_content - Assert Sports categories are visible      await mainPage.viewMoreSports();    });    await test.step('Discover Centres', async () => {      // Step: gxmtc - Scroll body      await mainPage.scrollBodyTo(0, 1444);      // Step: h1z8j9 - Click VIEW MORE CENTRES      // Step: h1z8j9_assert_centres_page - Assert navigation to centres page      await mainPage.viewMoreCentres();    });    await test.step('Navigate to Get Machaxi App page', async () => {      // Step: lajr3m - Navigate to https://machaxi.app.link/get-machaxi      // Step: lajr3m_assert_get_machaxi_url - Assert Get Machaxi app URL      await mainPage.navigateToGetMachaxiAppPage();    });    await test.step('Navigate to Play Store and add to wishlist', async () => {      // Step: k5sq2 - Scroll body      await mainPage.scrollBodyTo(0, 3888);      const playStoreAppUrl = 'https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.machaxi&_branch_match_id=1603653216442349552&utm_medium=marketing&_branch_referrer=H4sIAAAAAAAAA8soKSkottLXz01MzkisyNRLLCjQy8nMy9ZPTy3RhQra1xWlpqUWFWXmpccnFeWXF6cW2TpnFOXnpgIAnjri4D4AAAA%3D';      // Step: gelw04 - Navigate to Play Store URL      // Step: gelw04_assert_play_store_url - Assert Play Store URL      await mainPage.navigateToPlayStore(playStoreAppUrl);      // Step: fgsumk - Click Add to wishlist      // Step: fgsumk_assert_wishlist_added - Assert wishlist item added      // NOTE: Google Play Store might require login for 'Add to wishlist'.      // This step might fail if not logged in. For a robust test, user login      // would be handled first, or this step would be skipped/mocked for unauthenticated flows.      await mainPage.addToWishlist();    });    await test.step('Re-verify About Us and Play Store navigation', async () => {      // Step: 4i61cf - Navigate to About Us page again      // Step: 4i61cf_assert_about_us_url - Assert About Us URL      await mainPage.navigateToAboutUs();      // Step: 4naa - Scroll body      await mainPage.scrollBodyTo(0, 6519);      const playStoreAppUrl2 = 'https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.machaxi&pli=1';      // Step: 8yd1ee - Navigate to Play Store URL again      // Step: 8yd1ee_assert_play_store_url_2 - Assert Play Store URL      await mainPage.navigateToPlayStore(playStoreAppUrl2);    });    await test.step('Verify video pause functionality', async () => {      // Step: xm7sub - Navigate to About Us page      // Step: xm7sub_assert_about_us_url_2 - Assert About Us URL      await mainPage.navigateToAboutUs();      // Step: sjylc - Scroll body to top      await mainPage.scrollBodyTo(0, 0);      // Step: qlnmo7 - Click Pause video      // Step: qlnmo7_assert_video_paused - Assert Play video button is visible      await mainPage.assertVideoPaused();    });  });});

import { Page, Locator, expect } from '@playwright/test';export abstract class BasePage {  protected readonly page: Page;  constructor(page: Page) {    this.page = page;  }  async navigate(url: string): Promise<void> {    await this.page.goto(url);  }  async click(locator: Locator, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await locator.click(options);  }  async fill(locator: Locator, value: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await locator.fill(value, options);  }  async check(locator: Locator, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await locator.check(options);  }  async scroll(locator: Locator, x: number, y: number): Promise<void> {    await locator.evaluate((element, coords) => {      element.scrollTo(coords.x, coords.y);    }, { x, y });  }  async assertUrl(expectedUrl: string | RegExp, message?: string): Promise<void> {    await expect(this.page, message || `Expected URL to be ${expectedUrl}`).toHaveURL(expectedUrl);  }  async assertElementVisibility(locator: Locator, message?: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await expect(locator, message || `Expected element to be visible`).toBeVisible(options);  }  async assertElementText(locator: Locator, expectedText: string, message?: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await expect(locator, message || `Expected element to have text: ${expectedText}`).toHaveText(expectedText, options);  }  async assertElementIsChecked(locator: Locator, message?: string, options?: { timeout?: number }): Promise<void> {    await expect(locator, message || `Expected element to be checked`).toBeChecked(options);  }}

requests.name: Verify successful retrieval of a random joke
requests.description: Send a GET request to the /random_joke endpoint and ensure a 200 OK status code is returned with a valid joke object in the response body.
requests.expectedResults: HTTP status code is 200. The response body is a JSON object containing 'type', 'setup', 'punchline', and 'id' fields.

requests.name: Validate the JSON schema of the random joke response
requests.description: Verify that the response JSON object consistently contains the required fields: 'type', 'setup', 'punchline', and 'id', and that no critical fields are missing.
requests.expectedResults: The response JSON object strictly contains 'type', 'setup', 'punchline', and 'id' as top-level keys.

requests.description: Check that 'type', 'setup', and 'punchline' fields are strings, and the 'id' field is an integer.
requests.name: Validate data types of all fields in the random joke response
requests.expectedResults: The 'type', 'setup', and 'punchline' fields are strings, and the 'id' field is an integer.

requests.name: Verify joke content fields are non-empty
requests.description: Ensure that the 'setup' and 'punchline' fields in the response are not empty strings or null.
requests.expectedResults: The 'setup' and 'punchline' fields contain non-empty string values.
The API should return an appropriate error status code (e.g., 405 Method Not Allowed) for unsupported HTTP methods.
requests.name: Verify rejection of unsupported HTTP methods for random joke endpoint
requests.description: Attempt to send requests using HTTP methods other than GET (e.g., POST, PUT, DELETE) to the /random_joke endpoint.

requests.name: Verify Content-Type header is 'application/json'
requests.description: Check that the response from the /random_joke endpoint includes a 'Content-Type' header with the value 'application/json'.
requests.expectedResults: The 'Content-Type' header in the response is 'application/json'.

requests.name: Successful cart creation with valid `userId`, `date`, and a single product
requests.description: Send a POST request to /carts with a valid `userId`, `date` in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format, and a `products` array containing one item with valid `productId` and `quantity`.
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 200 OK or 201 Created status code. The response body should contain the newly created cart's details, including a unique `id`, and reflect the provided `userId`, `date`, and `products` array.
The API should return a 200 OK or 201 Created status code. The response body should contain the cart details, correctly listing all provided product items.
requests.description: Send a POST request to /carts with valid `userId`, `date`, and a `products` array containing multiple items, each with a distinct `productId` and `quantity`.
requests.name: Successful cart creation with multiple different products

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code and an error message indicating that `userId` is a required field.
requests.description: Send a POST request to /carts omitting the `userId` field from the request body.
requests.name: Error response when `userId` is missing from the request body

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code and an error message indicating that the `date` format is invalid or not parsable.
The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code and an error message indicating that at least one product is required for cart creation.

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code and an error message indicating that `productId` is required for each product item.

requests.description: Send a POST request to /carts with a product item having `quantity` as `0` or a negative value (e.g., `-1`).
requests.name: Error response for zero or negative `quantity` for a product item
requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code and an error message indicating that `quantity` must be a positive integer.
The API should ignore the extraneous fields, successfully create the cart, and return a 200 OK or 201 Created status code with the cart details reflecting only the known, provided fields.

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code and an error message indicating a malformed JSON payload.

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found status code, indicating that the resource identifier is malformed or invalid.

requests.name: Verify PUT request handling of invalid data types in the request body

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 200 OK status code. The response body should reflect the fields updated with empty string or null values as provided in the request.
requests.description: Send a PUT request to update an existing post, providing empty strings for 'title' and 'body', or explicitly 'null' for 'userId'.
requests.name: Verify PUT request with empty string or null values for fields

requests.expectedResults: The API should return a 400 Bad Request status code with an error message indicating an invalid JSON format.

requests.name: Verify successful partial update of 'title' field
